name: API-2500
description: Modeled API 2500 stereo bus compressor. VCA topology with Thrust circuit that filters bass from the detector for bass-preserving compression. Controls: Threshold, Attack (0.03-30ms), Release (0.05-3s), Ratio (1.5-10:1 plus Infinity), Knee (Old=hard, New=soft, both analog), Output Gain, Thrust (sidechain HPF). Character: punchy, aggressive, thick. Adds weight and slam. Choose over SSLComp when you want more aggressive punch on drum bus. Best for: drum bus (slam), rock/hip-hop mix bus, parallel compression, synth groups. Not ideal for transparent limiting or delicate vocals.

name: API-550A
description: Modeled API 550A 3-band EQ with proportional Q (Q narrows as boost increases — subtle boosts are broad, large boosts are focused). Fixed frequency points per band with 5 choices each. Band 1: 50-400Hz, Band 2: 0.4-3.2kHz, Band 3: 1.5-16kHz. +/-12dB per band. Character: punchy, bold, forward, never harsh. The API sound is thick and rock-oriented. Choose over Neve EQ when you want more aggressive, in-your-face midrange. Best for: drums (especially snare/toms), electric guitars, rock vocals. Less surgical than parametric EQs.

name: API-550B
description: Modeled API 550B 4-band EQ with proportional Q. Extended version of 550A with 4 bands instead of 3. Band 1: 30-400Hz, Band 2: 75Hz-2.5kHz, Band 3: 0.4-7kHz, Band 4: 2-20kHz. +/-12dB per band. Same punchy API character but more flexible with overlapping mid bands for detailed sculpting. Choose over 550A when you need finer midrange control with two mid bands. Best for: vocals needing both low-mid cleanup and upper-mid presence, full-range instruments, complex tonal shaping while keeping that bold API sound.

name: API-560
description: Modeled API 560 graphic EQ with 10 bands (31Hz to 16kHz, octave spacing). +/-12dB per band with proportional Q. Character: punchy, musical, fast workflow — just grab and push. No frequency/Q knobs to fiddle with. Choose over parametric EQs when you want fast, intuitive tonal shaping without overthinking. Best for: quick guitar tone fixes, drum overhead shaping, live-sound-style broad EQ moves, lo-fi character. Less precise than parametric but more musical and immediate for broad strokes.

name: Abbey Road Chambers
description: Convolution reverb capturing Abbey Road Studios' legendary STEED echo chambers — Room 1 (bright, tight), Room 2 (warm, medium), and the Mirror Room (long, lush). Uses actual impulse responses from the physical chambers. Controls: chamber select, mic position, speaker type (Altec/B&K), pre-delay, bass/treble cut, mix. Character: organic, vintage, musical — the real sound of countless classic records. Choose over algorithmic reverbs when you want authentic vintage studio ambience. Best for: vocals, strings, orchestral, piano, anything needing that classic 60s-70s Abbey Road depth.

name: Abbey Road EMI TG12345 Ch
description: Modeled EMI TG12345 channel strip from Abbey Road's TG console (installed 1968, used on Dark Side of the Moon, Abbey Road album). Sections: Mic Pre (with gain), EQ (Treble shelf, Presence, Bass shelf — each with frequency select), Compressor (with recovery/threshold), Limiter, HPF, LPF. Character: warm, rich, harmonically complex — adds beautiful coloration even at unity. The EQ has a unique 'glow' that flatters everything. Choose over SSL when you want warmth over clinical precision. Best for: vocals, drums, bass, full mixes wanting vintage British color.

name: Abbey Road J37 Tape
description: Modeled Abbey Road Studios' Studer J37 4-track tape machine (the actual unit used on Beatles recordings). 3 tape formulas: 888 (bright), 811 (warm), 815 (balanced). Controls: tape speed (7.5/15/30 IPS), bias, noise level, wow/flutter (depth + rate), delay, saturation, HF/LF adjustment. Character: rich harmonic warmth, gentle compression, HF smoothing, subtle pitch modulation. Higher speed = cleaner, lower speed = more saturation. Choose over Kramer Tape when you want historically authentic Beatles-era sound. Best for: drums, vocals, full mix bus — warming up harsh digital recordings.

name: Abbey Road Plates
description: Modeled EMT 140 plate reverbs from Abbey Road Studios — 4 distinct plates each with unique character. Controls: plate select (A/B/C/D), damper (decay time), pre-delay, bass/treble, drive (pushes into saturation), mix. Character: smooth, dense, lush decay with shimmering highs. Plate A is brightest, D is darkest. Drive control adds pleasant grit. Choose over H-Reverb when you want classic plate sound with less tweaking. Best for: vocals (plate reverb is THE classic vocal reverb), snare, percussion, pop/rock production. The most musical reverb type for most mixing situations.

name: Abbey Road REDD.17
description: Modeled REDD.17 valve (tube) console from Abbey Road Studios — the desk used on early Beatles records (Please Please Me through Revolver). Sections: preamp with gain, 3-band EQ (Bass/Mid/Treble), compressor/limiter. Character: warm, thick, richly harmonic tube saturation even at unity gain. Very colored — everything sounds warmer and more 'vintage' through it. Choose over REDD.37/51 when you want the most colored, tube-saturated vintage sound. Best for: rock vocals needing vintage warmth, acoustic instruments, anything where you want heavy vintage coloration.

name: Abbey Road REDD.37.51
description: Modeled REDD.37 and REDD.51 consoles from Abbey Road Studios — transitional desks between REDD.17 and TG (late Beatles era). Transistor-based rather than valve. Sections: preamp, 3-band EQ, compressor/limiter. Character: more punchy and aggressive than REDD.17 but still vintage. Less tube warmth, more transistor edge. Choose over REDD.17 when you want vintage character with more bite and definition. Best for: rock drums, electric guitars, bass — anything needing vintage edge rather than vintage warmth.

name: Abbey Road RS124
description: Modeled RS124 compressor from Abbey Road Studios — modified Altec 436B tube compressor. Three distinct units available: 'Peter' (smooth, gentle), 'Paul' (medium, balanced), 'George' (aggressive, more compression). Controls: input gain, recovery (release), superFuse, hold, mix. Character: smooth, warm tube compression with beautiful harmonic saturation. Program-dependent timing. Choose over CLA-2A when you want more tube warmth and vintage Abbey Road flavor. Best for: vocals, bass, acoustic guitar, room mics, bus compression wanting vintage tube glue.

name: Abbey Road RS56 Passive EQ
description: Modeled RS56 Universal Tone Control (Curve Bender) from Abbey Road — an extremely rare passive tube EQ. 6 bands: LF, LMF, MF, HMF, HF, plus HPF/LPF. Each band has frequency, gain, and Q controls. Character: incredibly smooth, silky, never harsh — passive EQ with tube amplification means the curves are very musical. Choose over active EQs when you want the smoothest possible EQ moves, especially for mastering. Best for: mastering, mix bus sweetening, acoustic instruments, classical/jazz — any situation where you need EQ that sounds 'invisible'.

name: Abbey Road Reel ADT
description: Emulation of Abbey Road's Automatic Double Tracking tape effect, invented by Ken Townsend for the Beatles (1966). Creates doubling by varying tape speed. Controls: LFO rate, depth, drive, dry/wet, varispeed modulation. Character: organic, natural-sounding doubling with subtle pitch/time modulation — much more realistic than simple delay-based doubling. Choose over Doubler when you want authentic tape-based doubling rather than pitch-shift doubling. Best for: lead vocals (thickening without chorus artifacts), guitars, keyboards, any source needing realistic double-tracking.

name: Abbey Road Reel ADT2V
description: Two-voice version of Abbey Road Reel ADT with independent control over two ADT voices. Each voice has separate rate, depth, and drive controls. Allows stereo widening by panning voices. Character: same authentic tape doubling but with stereo dimension. Choose over single-voice ADT when you want stereo spread from doubling, or creative effects with two different modulation speeds. Best for: stereo vocal widening, guitar stereo spread, synth pads, creating wide stereo image from mono sources.

name: Abbey Road Saturator
description: Analog saturation modeler with multiple saturation types. Controls: Drive (amount), Mix (parallel blend), output, saturation type select. Different types model various analog sources (tube, tape, transformer). Character: ranges from subtle warmth to aggressive grit depending on drive and type. Choose over dedicated tape/tube plugins when you want flexible saturation that can morph between different analog characters. Best for: drums (adding bite), bass (harmonic presence), vocals (warmth), mix bus (analog glue), any source needing controlled harmonic enhancement.

name: Abbey Road Studio 3
description: 3D headphone monitoring plugin recreating Abbey Road Studio 3 control room using Nx head-tracking technology. Simulates speakers, room acoustics, and head movement for accurate stereo/surround monitoring on headphones. Controls: head tracking, room simulation, speaker selection, headphone compensation. This is a MONITORING tool — use it for mixing, not for processing. Best for: mixing on headphones when you can't use speakers, checking mixes in a virtual reference room.

name: Abbey Road TG Mastering
description: Mastering chain based on EMI TG12410 transfer console at Abbey Road. Sections: HPF/LPF filters, Presence EQ, Tone EQ (shelving), Compressor (with sidechain filter), Limiter. Each section can be independently bypassed. Character: transparent yet musical — more subtle than the TG12345 channel strip. The EQ has a refined, gentle touch ideal for mastering moves. Choose over individual plugins when you want a cohesive mastering chain with consistent tonal character. Best for: mastering, mixdown finalization, stereo bus processing.

name: Abbey Road TG Meter Bridge
description: Metering plugin modeled after Abbey Road's TG console meter bridge. Provides VU, Peak, and Phase metering with classic console aesthetics. Analysis/monitoring tool only — does NOT process audio. Use for visual monitoring of levels, dynamics, and stereo balance during mixing and mastering.

name: Abbey Road The King's Microphones
description: EQ based on vintage microphone characteristics from Abbey Road's collection. Imparts the tonal fingerprint of legendary microphones including Neumann U47, U67, AKG C12, Coles 4038, and more. Controls: mic model select, intensity. Character: each mic model adds its unique frequency response curve. Choose when you want to add the character of expensive vintage mics to recordings made with ordinary mics. Best for: vocals, acoustic instruments — transforming the tonal character of any source to sound like it was recorded through a different microphone.

name: Abbey Road Vinyl
description: Vinyl record emulation with comprehensive modeling of the vinyl playback chain. Sections: Noise (surface noise, crackle intensity), Electrical (50/60Hz hum), Mechanical (wow, flutter, rumble), Frequency Response (vinyl curve). Controls per section for detailed vintage character. Choose over Abbey Road Vinyl Light when you need full control over every aspect of vinyl degradation. Best for: lo-fi hip-hop, vintage aesthetics, sound design, making modern recordings sound like vinyl pressings. Apply to individual tracks or mix bus.

name: Abbey Road Vinyl Light
description: Simplified version of Abbey Road Vinyl with fewer controls for quick results. Key controls: noise amount, wow/flutter amount, main mix. Same core vinyl modeling but streamlined workflow. Choose over full Abbey Road Vinyl when you want quick vinyl character without deep parameter diving. Best for: quick lo-fi treatment, adding subtle vintage vibe, when CPU matters (lighter than full version).

name: Aphex Vintage Exciter
description: Modeled Aphex Aural Exciter Type III. Psychoacoustic harmonic enhancer that generates upper harmonics from existing audio content to add presence, air, and clarity without simply boosting EQ. Controls: Mix, Tune (frequency of excitation), Harmonics (amount of generation), Mode. Character: adds 'sparkle' and 'air' that cuts through a mix — the harmonics are generated, not boosted, so they add new brightness. Choose over high shelf EQ when simple EQ boost sounds harsh. Best for: vocals (adding air and presence), acoustic guitar, cymbals, mix bus brightness, dull recordings.

name: AudioTrack
description: Basic channel strip with 4-band parametric EQ (2 semi-parametric mids, HF/LF shelving), compressor (Threshold/Ratio/Attack/Release), and noise gate (Threshold/Range). Minimal CPU usage. Character: clean, transparent, no color — purely functional processing. Choose when you need basic channel processing with absolute minimum CPU load. Best for: utility processing, demos, sessions with very high track counts where CPU matters, quick rough mixing.

name: B360 5.0/Quad
description: Ambisonics B-Format to 5.0 surround decoder. Converts ambisonics signals to multi-channel surround. Technical utility for spatial audio production and VR audio. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 5.1/Quad
description: Ambisonics B-Format to 5.1 surround decoder. Converts ambisonics signals to 5.1 surround including LFE channel. Technical utility for immersive audio and VR. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 7.1/Quad
description: Ambisonics B-Format to 7.1 surround decoder. Converts ambisonics signals to 7.1 surround. Technical utility for large immersive audio formats. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 AmbiX-FuMa
description: Ambisonics format converter: AmbiX to FuMa. Converts between two different B-Format ambisonics standards. Technical utility for spatial audio format interoperability. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 FuMa-AmbiX
description: Ambisonics format converter: FuMa to AmbiX. Converts between two different B-Format ambisonics standards. Technical utility for spatial audio format interoperability. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 Mono/Quad
description: Ambisonics encoder: mono input to B-Format output. Positions a mono source in 3D ambisonics space with azimuth/elevation control. For VR and immersive audio production. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: B360 Stereo/Quad
description: Ambisonics encoder: stereo input to B-Format output. Positions a stereo source in 3D ambisonics space. For VR and immersive audio production. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: Bass Rider
description: Automatic bass level rider that maintains consistent bass volume without compression artifacts. Analyzes bass frequencies and applies sample-accurate gain adjustments to even out performance dynamics. Controls: Target range (min/max), Sensitivity, Rider speed, Vocal sidechain (ducks bass when vocals present). Character: transparent — it just evens out level, adds no coloration. Choose over compressor when you want level consistency without changing the bass tone or dynamics character. Best for: bass guitar (essential for keeping bass solid in a mix), synth bass, any bass-heavy source with inconsistent levels.

name: Berzerk Distortion
description: Creative multi-stage distortion with extreme range. 6 distortion shapes: Crush, Insane, Saturate, Fuzz, Rectify, Squeez. Features: feedback loop (creates chaotic self-oscillation), dynamics section (gate/compressor), filter, wet/dry mix. Controls: Drive, Shape, Feedback, Dynamics, Filter, Mix. Character: from subtle grit to complete destruction and experimental noise. Choose over subtle saturation plugins when you want aggressive, creative, or experimental distortion effects. Best for: EDM/electronic (harsh synths), industrial, experimental sound design, drum mangling, lo-fi destruction. NOT for subtle warming.

name: Brauer Motion
description: Auto-panner and stereo motion processor designed with mixer Michael Brauer. Creates circular, lateral, and complex motion paths. Controls: trigger mode (auto/sync/manual), speed, depth, motion shape (circle, X, random, etc.), pre-delay, drive. Character: adds constant movement and life to static sounds, creating depth and width. Choose over simple pan automation when you want complex, evolving stereo motion. Best for: guitars, synths, pads, percussion, background vocals — any element that sounds static and needs life and movement in the stereo field.

name: Butch Vig Vocals
description: All-in-one vocal processing chain designed with producer Butch Vig (Nirvana, Smashing Pumpkins, Garbage). Sections: Compressor (with character knob), EQ (with presence/body), De-Esser, Reverb, Delay, Stereo widening. Each section has dedicated on/off. Character: modern rock vocal sound — upfront, present, compressed with character. Choose over individual plugins when you want a quick, complete rock vocal chain. Best for: rock vocals, alternative vocals, punk vocals, aggressive vocal styles. Less suited for delicate jazz/classical vocals.

name: C1 comp
description: Versatile single-band compressor with comprehensive control set. Controls: Threshold, Ratio (1:1-50:1), Attack (0.01-500ms), Release (1-5000ms), Gain, PDR (Program-Dependent Release), HPF sidechain filter. Transparent, clinical character — adds minimal coloration. Choose over colored compressors (CLA-76, CLA-2A) when you want purely transparent dynamic control. Best for: surgical compression where you don't want character added, utility compression, processing where the compressor should be invisible.

name: C1 comp-gate
description: Combined compressor and gate in one plugin. Same compressor as C1 plus integrated noise gate with Threshold, Floor, Attack, Release. Sidechain filter shared between comp and gate. Character: clean, transparent dual processing. Choose when a track needs both gating (noise removal) and compression in one insert, saving CPU and simplifying routing. Best for: live recordings needing cleanup + compression, drum tracks with bleed needing gating + dynamics control.

name: C1 comp-sc
description: C1 compressor with external sidechain input capability. Same clean compressor with full sidechain control — route any audio to trigger compression. Controls include sidechain filter (HPF/LPF) for frequency-selective triggering. Choose when you need sidechain compression (ducking). Best for: bass ducking from kick, vocal ducking from music, EDM sidechain pumping effect, de-essing with external sidechain, any frequency-triggered dynamic control.

name: C1 gate
description: Versatile noise gate with look-ahead, sidechain filter, and adjustable Floor. Controls: Threshold, Floor (how much to attenuate), Attack, Hold, Release, HPF/LPF sidechain filter. Character: clean, precise gating with zero coloration. Choose when you need surgical noise removal with full control. Best for: drum tracks (isolating kicks/snares from bleed), removing background noise, tightening up live recordings, any source where you need precise gating control.

name: C4
description: 4-band multiband dynamics processor. Each band has: Threshold, Range (compression/expansion amount), Attack, Release, Gain. Crossover frequencies adjustable. Bands can compress OR expand independently. Character: transparent multiband control. Choose over C6 when 4 bands is sufficient (less CPU, simpler). Best for: mastering (spectral dynamics control), taming resonant problem areas, de-essing without a de-esser, controlling muddy bass without EQ, frequency-specific dynamic management.

name: C6
description: 6-band multiband dynamics processor — 4 crossover bands plus 2 floating parametric bands for surgical control. Each band: Threshold, Range, Attack, Release, Gain, Solo. The 2 floating bands can target any frequency with adjustable Q. Character: extremely precise, transparent dynamics. Choose over C4 when you need the surgical floating bands for problem frequencies. Best for: mastering (the floating bands are perfect for taming specific resonances), live sound, de-essing, de-mudding, complex spectral dynamics problems.

name: C6-SideChain
description: C6 multiband dynamics with external sidechain input. Same 6-band processor but compression/expansion can be triggered by external audio. Each band can be individually sidechained. Choose when you need frequency-selective ducking triggered by another source. Best for: multiband sidechain (e.g., only duck bass frequencies from kick while leaving mids/highs untouched), multiband vocal ducking, broadcast processing, advanced frequency-aware dynamic routing.

name: CLA Bass
description: Bass processing chain by mix legend Chris Lord-Alge. Simple, effective controls: Sub (sub-bass), Low (bass body), High (top end presence), Compress (dynamics), Distort (harmonic grit). Also HPF and Treble controls. Character: punchy, full, radio-ready bass sound — CLA's signature bass treatment. Choose when you want quick, polished bass without tweaking multiple plugins. Best for: bass guitar in rock/pop, synth bass, any bass source needing quick professional treatment. Not for surgical precision work.

name: CLA Drums
description: Drum processing chain by Chris Lord-Alge. Controls: Bite (transient/attack enhancement), Squash (heavy compression), Compress (moderate compression), Fatten (low-end weight), Sub. Character: punchy, aggressive, radio-ready drum sound. CLA's Grammy-winning drum treatment in one plugin. Choose when you want quick, professional drum processing without detailed tweaking. Best for: drum bus, individual drums in rock/pop, aggressive drum sounds. Not for subtle jazz or acoustic drum treatment.

name: CLA EchoSphere
description: Combined delay + reverb designed by Chris Lord-Alge. Sections: Delay (with filtering, modulation, sync), Reverb (multiple types), Chorus. Each section independently on/off. Character: warm, musical spatial effects tuned by CLA. Choose over separate delay+reverb when you want a quick, cohesive vocal space effect. Best for: vocal ambience (CLA's specialty), guitar space, synth depth — any source needing delay+reverb as one cohesive effect.

name: CLA Effects
description: Multi-effects processor by Chris Lord-Alge combining distortion, delay, reverb, phaser, flanger, and more. Multiple effect slots with CLA-curated presets. Character: creative, musical effects with CLA's sonic signature. Choose when you want quick creative effects without building complex chains. Best for: creative vocal effects, guitar processing, synth enhancement, adding character to any source with CLA's signature style.

name: CLA Epic
description: Large-format delay and reverb by Chris Lord-Alge designed for cinematic, dramatic spatial effects. Features long tails, deep modulation, and expansive stereo imaging. Controls: Delay section (feedback, filtering, sync), Reverb section (size, decay, damping), Throw controls for dramatic delay throws. Character: huge, cinematic, epic space. Choose over subtle reverbs when you want BIG, dramatic spatial effects. Best for: vocal throws, snare reverb explosions, cinematic builds, dramatic breakdowns, massive guitar ambience.

name: CLA Guitars
description: Guitar processing chain by Chris Lord-Alge. Controls: Bite (presence/attack), Body (low-mid fullness), Treble (high-end sparkle), Compress (dynamics), Distort (edge/grit). Character: professional, radio-ready guitar tone — CLA's signature guitar processing. Choose when you want quick professional guitar polish. Best for: electric guitar in rock/pop/alternative, guitar bus processing, quick guitar enhancement. Not for amp simulation or acoustic guitar.

name: CLA MixDown
description: Stereo mix bus processor by Chris Lord-Alge. Complete final chain: EQ section (bass, mid, treble shaping), Compression (bus glue), Stereo Enhancement (width control), Limiting (final loudness). Character: polished, loud, radio-ready master bus processing with CLA's signature aggressive clarity. Choose when you want quick mix finalization with one plugin. Best for: mix bus (the primary use case), submix bus processing, quick mastering for demos.

name: CLA MixHub
description: Full console emulation by Chris Lord-Alge modeling his actual analog console signal path. Sections: Input (preamp with drive), EQ (3-band with character), Compressor (with multiple modes), Mix Bus routing. Multiple console models available. Character: analog console warmth, depth, and cohesion — like mixing through a real console. Choose over individual channel strip plugins when you want the full CLA console experience. Best for: every track in a mix (use on all channels for console cohesion), adding analog console depth and width.

name: CLA MixHub Lite
description: Simplified version of CLA MixHub console emulation with fewer controls and lower CPU. Core console processing: preamp drive, basic EQ, compression. Character: same CLA console vibe but streamlined. Choose over full MixHub when CPU matters or you want faster workflow. Best for: large sessions where full MixHub is too heavy, quick console character on every channel.

name: CLA Nx
description: Headphone monitoring plugin simulating Chris Lord-Alge's mixing environment using Nx head-tracking technology. Recreates the acoustic environment of CLA's mix room on headphones. MONITORING tool only — does not process audio for the mix. Best for: mixing on headphones with a reference to CLA's monitoring environment.

name: CLA Unplugged
description: Acoustic instrument processor by Chris Lord-Alge. Optimized for acoustic guitars, pianos, strings, and other unplugged sources. Controls: Body (low end), Treble (top end), Compress (dynamics), Ambience (room/reverb), additional tonal controls. Character: warm, present, polished acoustic sound. Choose when you want quick professional treatment for acoustic instruments. Best for: acoustic guitar, piano, strings, any unplugged instrument in pop/rock/folk productions.

name: CLA Vocals
description: Vocal processing chain by Chris Lord-Alge. Controls: Bass (low end body), Treble (presence/air), Compress (dynamics), Reverb (space), Delay (echo), Pitch (subtle correction). All sections independently adjustable. Character: upfront, present, radio-ready vocal sound — CLA's signature vocal treatment used on countless hits. Choose when you want quick, polished vocal processing. Best for: lead vocals in pop/rock/alternative, background vocals, vocal bus. The fastest way to get a professional vocal sound.

name: CLA-2A
description: Modeled Teletronix LA-2A optical compressor. Controls are deceptively simple: Gain (output), Peak Reduction (threshold/ratio combined), and Comp/Limit switch. The optical (T4B cell) detection gives program-dependent attack/release that adapts to the audio — slow attack on transients, fast recovery on sustained material. Character: smooth, warm, musical, never aggressive. The most 'invisible' compression possible while still being effective. Choose over CLA-76 when you want smooth, transparent compression. Choose over CLA-3A for slower, silkier compression. Best for: vocals (#1 vocal compressor in history), bass, acoustic guitar, mix bus. NOT ideal for fast transients (drums) or aggressive pumping.

name: CLA-3A
description: Modeled UREI LA-3A optical compressor. Solid-state version of the optical compressor concept (faster than LA-2A). Controls: Gain, Peak Reduction, Attack/Release characteristics fixed but faster than 2A. Character: more aggressive and faster than CLA-2A but still smooth optical compression. Adds slightly more presence and 'grab'. Choose over CLA-2A when you need faster optical compression with more bite. Choose over CLA-76 when you want something between 2A smoothness and 76 aggression. Best for: electric guitar, snare drum, faster vocals, bass guitar, anything needing optical compression with more urgency than the 2A.

name: CLA-76
description: Modeled UREI 1176 FET compressor — the most versatile and widely-used compressor in recording history. Controls: Input (drives threshold), Output, Attack (fastest full clockwise = 20μs to slowest at 800μs), Release (fastest full clockwise = 50ms to slowest at 1.1s), Ratio (4/8/12/20:1), plus famous All-Buttons-In mode (all ratios pushed = extreme limiting). REVERSE knob logic: full CW = fastest. FET circuit gives aggressive, fast, exciting sound with harmonic distortion that adds presence. Choose over CLA-2A when you need speed, punch, and aggression. Choose over SSLComp for individual tracks vs bus. Best for: vocals (exciting, present), drums (punchy), bass (defined), guitars, synths — works on literally everything. The #1 all-purpose compressor.

name: Center
description: Stereo utility extracting or adjusting center (mono) vs side (stereo) content. Controls: Center level, Sides level, Punch (center dynamics), crossover. Separates stereo signals into center and sides components for independent control. Choose when you need to adjust the balance between centered elements (vocal, kick, snare, bass) and stereo elements (reverb, guitars, pads). Best for: rebalancing mixes, reducing/boosting vocals in stereo mixes, widening or narrowing stereo image, karaoke (vocal removal), mastering width adjustments.

name: Clarity Vx
description: AI-powered vocal noise reduction using neural networks trained on millions of vocal samples. Single main control: noise reduction amount. Automatically identifies and removes background noise (room tone, HVAC, street noise, equipment hum) while preserving voice quality. Character: transparent — just removes noise without affecting the vocal. Choose over traditional noise reduction (X-Noise, Z-Noise) for vocals specifically — AI-based approach is far more natural. Best for: podcast vocals, dialogue cleanup, vocal recordings in untreated rooms, remote recording cleanup, any vocal with background noise.

name: Clarity Vx - DeReverb
description: AI-powered reverb removal from recordings. Uses neural networks to identify and reduce unwanted room reverb and ambience while preserving the dry signal. Single main control: amount of reverb reduction. Character: remarkably transparent — removes reverb tail without metallic artifacts common in older tech. Choose over conventional gating for reverb issues. Best for: cleaning up vocals recorded in reverberant rooms, dialogue recorded on-set (film/TV), home studio recordings with room problems, improving clarity of reverb-heavy recordings.

name: Clarity Vx - DeReverb Pro
description: Advanced AI reverb removal with more control than standard DeReverb. Additional controls: frequency-dependent reverb reduction, early reflections vs tail control, sensitivity adjustment. More CPU-heavy but more precise. Choose over standard DeReverb when you need fine-tuned control over reverb removal, especially for difficult cases. Best for: professional post-production, film dialogue, complex reverb situations where standard DeReverb isn't enough, high-quality audio restoration.

name: Clarity Vx Pro
description: Advanced AI noise reduction with more control than standard Clarity Vx. Features: multiple noise reduction algorithms, frequency-dependent processing, learn mode for custom noise profiles, ambience preservation control. Choose over standard Clarity Vx when you need more precise control over noise reduction or have complex noise situations. Best for: professional broadcast, high-end post-production, extreme noise situations, environments with changing noise profiles.

name: Curves AQ
description: AI-powered adaptive EQ that learns from reference audio. Analyzes your audio and a target reference, then automatically creates an EQ curve to match. Controls: match intensity, frequency range, smoothing, manual EQ override bands. Character: transparent EQ matching — goal is to make your audio sound like the reference. Choose when you have a reference track and want to match its tonal balance. Best for: mastering (matching reference), ensuring tonal consistency across albums, quickly correcting tonal imbalances, learning/teaching EQ by seeing what a reference does differently.

name: Curves Equator
description: AI-powered adaptive dynamics that learns from reference material. Analyzes dynamic range, envelope shape, and loudness profile of a target, then matches your audio to it. Controls: match intensity, dynamics range, attack/release influence. Character: intelligent dynamics matching — automatically applies the right compression to match a reference. Choose when you want your dynamics to match a reference track. Best for: mastering, achieving commercial loudness/dynamics balance, learning dynamics processing by comparing to references.

name: Curves Resolve
description: AI-powered resonance detection and removal. Automatically scans audio for problematic resonances (ringing frequencies, room modes, harsh peaks) and notches them out. Controls: sensitivity, resolution, reduction amount, frequency range. Character: surgical, transparent — targets only the problems. Choose over manual notch EQ when you want automatic resonance hunting. Best for: room resonance removal, taming harsh guitar feedback, cleaning up resonant drum sounds, dialogue cleanup, any source with problematic ringing frequencies.

name: DPR-402
description: Modeled BSS DPR-402 professional dynamics processor. Dual-mode: Compressor + De-Esser in one unit. Compressor: Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Gain. De-Esser: frequency select, threshold, HF limiting. Character: transparent, broadcast-grade dynamics. Choose when you need both compression and de-essing in one plugin with broadcast precision. Best for: voice-over, broadcast, dialogue (designed for broadcast chain), vocals needing simultaneous compression and de-essing.

name: DeBreath
description: Automatic breath removal for vocal recordings. AI-powered breath detection with controls: Sensitivity (breath detection threshold), Reduction (how much to attenuate breaths, -inf to 0dB), Energy (response speed). Can remove breaths entirely or just reduce them for natural results. Character: transparent — affects only breaths. Choose over manual editing when you need fast, consistent breath management across many vocal tracks. Best for: podcasts, audiobooks, voice-over, pop vocals, any vocal recording where breaths are distracting. Set reduction to -6 to -12dB for natural results rather than full removal.

name: DeEsser
description: Classic frequency-selective de-esser for sibilance control. Controls: Threshold, Frequency (target sibilance range, typically 4-10kHz), Sidechain monitor (audio/wideband/sidechain). Broadband or split-band modes. Character: simple, effective, slightly colored. Choose over Sibilance when you want a traditional de-esser approach (threshold-based). Choose Sibilance for more natural, intelligent de-essing. Best for: vocals with harsh 's' and 'sh' sounds, cymbals that are too bright, any source with problematic high-frequency energy in a specific range.

name: Doppler
description: Doppler effect simulator recreating the pitch shift, volume change, and filtering of a sound source passing by the listener at variable speeds. Controls: Speed, Distance, Path shape (fly-by, approach, recede), Air filtering, Drive, Mix. Character: realistic motion simulation with physics-based modeling. Choose when you want the specific Doppler effect (pitch drops as object passes). Best for: sound design (cars, planes, sirens), creative effects (synth fly-bys), cinematic whooshes, post-production motion effects.

name: Dorrough
description: Modeled Dorrough 280-D loudness meter — broadcast industry standard. Displays simultaneous Peak and Average (persistent/summary) on a single scale. Multiple ballistic modes. METERING/ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY — does not process audio. Best for: broadcast compliance monitoring, mastering level monitoring, understanding the relationship between peak and average loudness.

name: Doubler2
description: 2-voice doubler creating natural-sounding doubling using pitch shifting and delay. Controls per voice: Detune (pitch shift amount), Delay, Pan, Level, Feedback. Global: direct level, EQ. Character: thickening and widening through micro pitch/time differences. Choose over ADT when you want simpler, modern doubling. Choose 4-voice Doubler4 for thicker results. Best for: vocal thickening, guitar widening, synth fattening, background vocal spread, adding stereo width to mono sources.

name: Doubler4
description: 4-voice doubler for thick doubling effects. Same concept as Doubler2 but with 4 independent pitch-shifted/delayed voices for much richer results. Controls per voice: Detune, Delay, Pan, Level. Character: lush, thick ensemble effect from the 4 detuned voices. Choose over Doubler2 when you want thicker doubling, or for creating wide vocal stacks. Best for: big background vocal sounds, thick guitar walls, synth pad widening, creating rich ensemble effects from a single source.

name: EKramer BA
description: Bass amp processor by legendary producer/engineer Eddie Kramer (Hendrix, Led Zeppelin, Beatles). Models classic bass amplifier tones with EQ, compression, drive, and cab simulation. Character: warm, vintage rock bass — the sound of classic records. Choose when you want quick vintage bass amp tones. Best for: bass guitar DI recordings needing amp character, vintage rock bass sounds, synth bass needing analog amp warmth.

name: EKramer DR
description: Drum processor by Eddie Kramer. Controls optimized for drums: compression, EQ, room simulation, drive. Character: big, punchy, room-filling drum sound — classic rock drum processing by the man who recorded Led Zeppelin's drums. Choose when you want classic rock drum production style. Best for: drum bus, room mics, overhead processing, individual drums in rock/classic rock context.

name: EKramer FX
description: Multi-effects processor by Eddie Kramer. Combines delay, reverb, phaser, flanger, chorus in a vintage-flavored effects rack. Each effect has Eddie Kramer's curated settings. Character: vintage-flavored creative effects. Choose when you want quick vintage spatial/modulation effects. Best for: guitar effects, vocal effects, creative vintage-style processing, achieving 60s-70s production aesthetics.

name: EKramer GT
description: Guitar amp processor by Eddie Kramer. Models classic guitar amplifier tones with amp selection, EQ, drive, and cabinet simulation. Character: classic rock guitar — Hendrix, Zeppelin tones. Choose when you want vintage rock guitar amp simulation. Best for: electric guitar DI recordings, achieving classic rock guitar sounds, Hendrix-style tones.

name: EKramer VC
description: Vocal channel processor by Eddie Kramer. Complete vocal chain: preamp drive, compression, EQ, doubling, reverb. Designed around Eddie Kramer's vocal recording techniques from classic records. Character: warm, present, vintage vocal sound. Choose when you want a vintage-style complete vocal chain. Best for: rock vocals, classic-style vocal productions, vocals needing vintage warmth and character.

name: EMO-D5
description: Emotion Series dynamics processor combining 5 modules: Gate, Leveler, De-Esser, Compressor, Limiter. All in one compact interface. Each module can be independently enabled/disabled. Character: clean, efficient multi-stage dynamics. Choose when you need a complete dynamics chain in minimal CPU/interface space. Best for: live sound (compact chain), quick studio dynamics setup, vocal chains needing gate+comp+de-esser+limiter in one.

name: EMO-F2
description: Emotion Series 2-band parametric filter. Simple hi-pass and lo-pass filters with frequency and Q control. Minimal CPU. Character: clean, purely functional filtering. Choose when you just need simple hi/lo pass filtering. Best for: utility filtering, rumble removal (HPF), harsh top-end removal (LPF), quick cleanup with minimal CPU overhead.

name: EMO-Generator
description: Test tone and noise generator. Produces: sine wave (variable frequency), pink noise, white noise, impulse. Controls: frequency, level, signal type. UTILITY TOOL — not for music production. Best for: system calibration, signal path testing, room acoustics measurement, troubleshooting audio equipment.

name: EMO-Q4
description: Emotion Series 4-band parametric EQ. Each band: Frequency, Gain (+/-18dB), Q (0.5-15). Plus HPF and LPF. Character: clean, transparent, zero coloration — purely functional EQ. Choose when you want simple, clean EQ without any analog modeling or character. Best for: utility EQ, live sound (efficient), basic tonal corrections where you don't want any plugin character.

name: Enigma
description: Creative multi-effect combining resonant filtering, modulation (LFO/envelope follower), delay, and feedback into a complex effect chain. Controls: Filter (frequency, resonance, type), Modulation (LFO rate, depth, shape), Delay (time, feedback), Feedback routing. Character: otherworldly, psychedelic, constantly evolving textures. Choose when you want complex, experimental modulation effects. Best for: experimental sound design, psychedelic guitar effects, ambient synth textures, creating evolving, unpredictable sonic textures.

name: F6
description: 6-band floating-point dynamic EQ with real-time frequency analyzer. Each band can act as standard EQ OR dynamic EQ (compress/expand at that frequency). Controls per band: Frequency, Gain, Q, Range (dynamic amount), Threshold, Attack, Release. RTA display shows frequency content in real-time. Character: surgical, precise, transparent. The most problem-solving EQ available. Choose over H-EQ when you need dynamic EQ (frequency-specific compression). Choose over C6 when you want visual feedback. Best for: problem-solving (resonance taming, frequency-dependent dynamics), mastering, de-essing with visual feedback, live vocals, any complex tonal problem.

name: F6-RTA
description: F6 dynamic EQ with enhanced real-time frequency analyzer display. Same powerful 6-band dynamic EQ as F6 but with more detailed RTA visualization. Choose over F6 when the visual analysis is important for your workflow. Best for: same applications as F6 but when you want better visual frequency feedback — mastering, problem-solving, live sound with visual monitoring.

name: Feedback Hunter
description: Automatic feedback detection and elimination for live sound. Scans for feedback frequencies and places precise notch filters to suppress them. Controls: sensitivity, number of filters, Q of notch filters, auto/manual mode. Character: transparent — notch filters are tight enough to be inaudible on the program material. Choose when you have feedback issues in live sound or monitoring. Best for: live sound reinforcement (essential), stage monitor mixing, PA system optimization, house of worship audio.

name: GEQ Classic
description: 30-band graphic EQ with classic analog-modeled response (1/3 octave spacing from 25Hz to 20kHz). +/-12dB per band. Analog modeling means bands interact slightly like a real analog graphic EQ. Character: musical, slightly colored — bands affect each other like hardware. Choose over GEQ Modern when you want analog-style graphic EQ behavior. Best for: live sound system tuning, quick broad tonal shaping, venue EQ, monitor mixing — any situation where fast, visual EQ is needed.

name: GEQ Modern
description: 30-band graphic EQ with linear-phase digital response (1/3 octave spacing). +/-12dB per band. True linear-phase processing means zero phase distortion and bands don't interact. Character: transparent, precise, clinically clean. Choose over GEQ Classic when phase accuracy matters (mastering, critical applications). Best for: mastering, high-fidelity system tuning, critical applications where phase distortion is unacceptable.

name: GTR Amp
description: Guitar amp simulator with multiple amp models covering clean to high-gain. Models include classic American (Fender-style), British (Marshall-style), and modern high-gain amps. Controls: Amp select, Gain, EQ (Bass/Mid/Treble), Volume, Cabinet select. Character: depends on amp model — ranges from clean sparkle to heavy crunch. Choose when you need guitar amp simulation for DI-recorded guitar. Best for: DI guitar recordings, re-amping, guitar processing without a real amp.

name: GTR Amp 2Cab
description: Guitar amp simulator with dual cabinet selection. Same amp modeling as GTR Amp but allows blending two different speaker cabinets for richer, more complex tones. Choose over GTR Amp when you want more tonal variety from cabinet blending. Best for: achieving complex guitar tones through cabinet layering, vintage + modern cab combinations.

name: GTR Solo Tool Rack
description: Complete guitar effects and amp rack in single-instance format. Combines stomp effects + amp + cabinet in one plugin. Streamlined for lead guitar processing. Best for: quick complete guitar rig setup for lead guitar parts.

name: GTR Stomp 2
description: 2-slot guitar stomp box effects rack. Includes various pedal models: overdrive, distortion, fuzz, chorus, flanger, phaser, delay, reverb, wah, compressor. Chain 2 pedals in series. Best for: simple guitar pedalboard setups, adding 1-2 effects to a guitar signal.

name: GTR Stomp 4
description: 4-slot guitar stomp box effects rack. Same pedal models as Stomp 2 but with 4 slots for more complex pedalboard configurations. Best for: moderate guitar pedalboard setups, typical live guitar effects chains.

name: GTR Stomp 6
description: 6-slot guitar stomp box effects rack. Full pedalboard with 6 effects slots for complex guitar processing chains. Best for: comprehensive guitar pedalboard emulation, complex effects chains, recreating real pedalboard setups in software.

name: GTR Tool Rack
description: Complete guitar rig: stomp effects + amp + cabinet + tuner in one plugin. The full solution for guitar processing from effects through amp simulation to cabinet modeling. Choose over separate stomp/amp plugins when you want everything in one interface. Best for: complete guitar rig replacement, home recording, live performance guitar processing.

name: GTR Tuner
description: Chromatic guitar/bass tuner. Displays pitch with cent accuracy. Simple, accurate tuning reference. UTILITY TOOL. Best for: tuning guitars, bass, and other chromatic instruments.

name: GW MixCentric
description: Mix bus processor by Grammy-winning producer Greg Wells (Adele, Katy Perry, OneRepublic). All-in-one mix finalization: compression, EQ, stereo enhancement, low-end control, limiting. Character: polished, modern pop/rock — huge but controlled. Choose when you want a quick, professional mix bus chain with a modern pop production aesthetic. Best for: mix bus processing, pop/rock/indie mix finalization, stereo bus sweetening. One of the best one-plugin mix bus solutions.

name: GW PianoCentric
description: Piano-specific processor by Greg Wells. Dedicated EQ curves, compression, and spatial processing optimized for piano. Controls tuned specifically to piano frequency ranges and dynamics. Character: clear, present, musical piano sound. Choose when mixing piano in pop/rock contexts — Greg Wells' piano sounds are legendary. Best for: piano in pop/rock/indie, piano-driven songs, piano bus processing.

name: GW ToneCentric
description: Saturation and tonal enhancement by Greg Wells. Adds harmonic richness with controls for intensity and character. Character: warm, full, modern analog warmth — Greg Wells' signature tonal sweetening. Choose over generic saturation when you want a specific, tested, modern production aesthetic. Best for: any source needing warmth and presence (vocals, drums, guitars, bus), mix bus analog sweetening, adding 'expensive analog console' character.

name: GW VoiceCentric
description: Vocal processor by Greg Wells. Complete vocal chain optimized for modern pop production: compression, EQ, presence enhancement, spatial processing. Character: clear, present, polished — the vocal sound of modern pop hits. Choose over CLA Vocals when you want modern pop production (CLA is more rock-oriented). Best for: pop vocals, R&B vocals, modern vocal production, lead vocals in commercial music.

name: H-Comp
description: Hybrid compressor combining analog modeling with digital precision. 4 analog character modes: Punchy (VCA-style), Smooth (optical-style), British (Neve-style transformer), and Clean (transparent). Controls: Threshold, Ratio, Attack (0.005-100ms), Release (1-3000ms), Mix (parallel compression built in!), Analog mode select. The built-in Mix knob is huge — instant parallel compression without routing. Character varies by mode: from transparent to heavily colored. Choose when you want versatile compression with easy parallel blending. Best for: drums (parallel compression with mix knob), vocals, bass, bus — the most flexible compressor for any situation.

name: H-Delay
description: Hybrid delay with analog-modeled character. Features: tempo sync, ping-pong mode, analog/digital mode, LoFi mode (bit-crush), filtering (HPF+LPF on feedback), modulation, ducking. Controls: Delay time (free/sync), Feedback, Mix, Filter, Modulation, Analog/Digital character. Character: ranges from pristine digital to warm analog to degraded lo-fi depending on settings. Choose when you need a versatile, full-featured delay. Best for: vocals (slapback, tempo delay), guitars (rhythmic delay), synths, any source — the most versatile all-purpose delay plugin. Set LoFi mode for tape-style degrading repeats.

name: H-EQ
description: Hybrid 7-band parametric EQ with switchable analog character models. 3 analog modes: British 60s/70s (Neve-style warmth), American 70s/80s (API-style punch), Modern (transparent digital). 7 bands: HP, LP, plus 5 parametric. Each band: Frequency, Gain, Q, band type (bell/shelf/cut). Character: adapts to the selected analog model — warm/punchy/transparent. Choose over dedicated vintage EQs when you want flexibility to switch between characters. Choose over F6 when you don't need dynamic EQ. Best for: everyday mixing EQ (the most versatile EQ), vocals, drums, guitars, bus — works on everything with adjustable character.

name: H-EQ-Light
description: Lightweight version of H-EQ with same 7 bands but simplified controls and lower CPU. Fewer display options, same sound quality. Choose over full H-EQ when CPU matters or you want faster workflow. Best for: large sessions, quick EQ adjustments, sessions where CPU is limited.

name: H-Reverb
description: Hybrid reverb engine combining algorithmic processing with FIR (Finite Impulse Response) technology for extremely dense, lush tails. Types: Hall, Room, Plate, Chamber, Ambience, Reverse, plus vintage analog reverb emulations. Controls: Type, Time (decay), Size, Damping, Pre-Delay, EQ, Modulation, Drive (pushable into saturation), Mix. Character: dense, smooth, professional — exceptionally lush decay tails. Choose over Abbey Road Plates when you want more variety and control. Choose over IR reverbs when you want tweakability. Best for: vocals (lush plate/hall), drums (room/ambient), synths (long tails), cinematic reverb, anything needing premium spatial treatment.

name: H-Reverb long
description: Extended decay version of H-Reverb with much longer maximum tail times. Same engine and controls as H-Reverb but allows decay times up to minutes. Choose over regular H-Reverb when you need very long, atmospheric reverb tails. Best for: ambient music, drone, atmospheric pads, cinematic sound design, infinite-style reverbs, special effects.

name: IDX Intelligent Dynamics
description: AI-driven intelligent multiband dynamics processor. Automatically analyzes audio content and applies optimal multiband compression, expansion, and EQ. Controls: Intensity, Style (transparent/aggressive), Focus (frequency emphasis). The AI engine adapts processing to the material in real-time. Choose over manual multiband dynamics when you want intelligent, automatic spectral dynamics. Best for: quick mastering, consistent dynamics across varying material, broadcast processing, time-saving dynamic control.

name: IDX LIVE Intelligent Dynamics
description: Low-latency version of IDX for live performance use. Same AI-driven multiband dynamics with minimal processing delay. Choose over studio IDX for live sound applications. Best for: live sound reinforcement, live broadcast, real-time vocal processing, any live application needing intelligent dynamics.

name: IMPusher
description: Mastering-grade loudness maximizer with intelligent multi-stage processing. Combines saturation, compression, and limiting for maximum loudness with minimal distortion. Controls: Push (loudness amount), Style (character), Ceiling, Output. Character: aggressive loudness without obvious artifacts — designed to push masters very loud. Choose over L2/L316 when you want to push loudness beyond traditional limiting. Best for: competitive loudness mastering, electronic music masters, hip-hop masters, any master that needs to be LOUD.

name: IR-L
description: Convolution reverb using impulse responses of real acoustic spaces. Full-featured IR reverb with extensive built-in IR library (halls, rooms, churches, studios, plates). Controls: IR select, Pre-Delay, Reverb Time scaling, Damping, Size, EQ, Mix. Character: utterly realistic — these are recordings of actual spaces. Choose over algorithmic reverbs when you want 100% realistic room simulation. Best for: orchestral (real halls), film scoring, realistic room simulation, drum room ambience, classical music.

name: IR-L efficient
description: CPU-efficient version of IR-L convolution reverb. Same impulse response quality with optimized processing. Choose over full IR-L when CPU budget is tight. Best for: same applications as IR-L but in CPU-constrained sessions.

name: IR-L full
description: Full-resolution IR-L convolution reverb with maximum processing quality. Higher CPU usage but maximum fidelity. Choose over efficient version for final mixes and mastering. Best for: critical applications, film scoring final mixes, mastering.

name: IR1
description: Convolution reverb with parametric control over impulse responses. Unique: allows tweaking IR properties (decay, size, damping) that normally can't be changed with convolution. Controls: IR select, Decay, Size, Pre-Delay, Damping, EQ, Density, Direct signal. Character: realistic with flexibility — the best of both convolution and algorithmic worlds. Choose over IR-L when you need to modify IR characteristics. Best for: any reverb application where you want realistic spaces but need to adapt them.

name: IR1 efficient
description: CPU-efficient version of IR1 parametric convolution reverb. Same tweakable convolution with lower CPU. Best for: same as IR1 but in CPU-constrained sessions.

name: IR1 full
description: Full-resolution IR1 parametric convolution reverb. Maximum quality processing. Best for: final mixes, mastering, critical applications.

name: IRLive
description: Low-latency convolution reverb for live sound applications. Real impulse responses with minimal processing delay. Choose over other IR reverbs when latency matters (live performance). Best for: live sound, live broadcast, monitoring with reverb, any real-time application needing realistic convolution reverb.

name: InPhase
description: Precision phase alignment and correction tool. Controls: phase shift (0-360° continuous), delay (samples/ms), HPF/LPF, correlation meter, waveform display. Aligns phase between two or more microphones/tracks with sample-accurate precision. Character: transparent — corrects phase without coloring sound. Choose when you have phase issues from multi-mic recording. Best for: multi-mic drum recordings (kick in/out, top/bottom snare), bass DI + amp alignment, acoustic guitar + room mic alignment, any multi-microphone situation.

name: InPhase LT
description: Simplified version of InPhase for basic phase correction. Same core functionality with fewer controls (no full waveform display). Choose over full InPhase for quick phase fixes. Best for: simple phase alignment tasks, quick phase flip, basic delay compensation.

name: InTrigger
description: Intelligent drum trigger and replacer. Detects drum hits and triggers replacement samples or sends MIDI. Controls: Sensitivity, Trigger frequency range, Retrigger time, Sample selection, Blend (original + sample mix), MIDI output settings. Character: transparent triggering — blends seamlessly with original. Choose for drum replacement/augmentation. Best for: reinforcing weak drum hits, replacing poorly recorded drums, layering samples with live drums, MIDI drum triggering for virtual instruments.

name: JJP-Bass
description: Bass processor by Jack Joseph Puig (Green Day, U2, Rolling Stones). Controls: Sub (sub-bass), Lo (bass body), Hi (presence), Attack (transient), Punch (compression), DI/Amp blend. Character: full, round, present bass — JJP's signature bass sound. Choose for quick professional bass processing. Best for: bass guitar in rock/pop/punk, synth bass, any bass source needing professional treatment.

name: JJP-Cymb-Perc
description: Cymbal and percussion processor by Jack Joseph Puig. Dedicated controls for cymbal/percussion frequency ranges: Body, Shimmer, Attack, Compression. Character: controlled, balanced cymbal/percussion sound — tames harshness while adding shimmer. Choose specifically for cymbal/percussion processing. Best for: drum overhead processing, cymbal bus, percussion bus, hi-hat control, taming harsh cymbal recordings.

name: JJP-Drums
description: Drum processor by Jack Joseph Puig. Controls: Punch (transient attack), Body (low-mid fullness), Crunch (distortion/edge), Room (ambience), HiHat (cymbal control). Character: big, punchy, full drum sound — JJP's signature rock drum treatment. Choose for quick professional drum processing. Best for: drum bus, individual drum processing in rock/pop/punk, aggressive drum sounds.

name: JJP-Guitars
description: Guitar processor by Jack Joseph Puig. Controls: Bite (high-mid presence), Body (low-mid fullness), Edge (distortion), Compress, Ambience. Character: upfront, cutting guitar sound — JJP's signature guitar tone heard on punk and rock records. Choose for quick professional guitar processing. Best for: electric guitar in rock/punk/alternative, guitar bus processing, guitars needing to cut through a dense mix.

name: JJP-Strings-Keys
description: Strings and keyboard processor by Jack Joseph Puig. Controls: Body (warmth/fullness), Treble (presence/air), Compress (dynamics), Ambience (space), Width (stereo spread). Optimized for piano, synth, strings, and pads. Character: rich, deep, present — makes keyboards sit beautifully in a mix. Best for: piano, synth pads, strings, organ, any keyboard instrument in pop/rock context.

name: JJP-Vocals
description: Vocal processor by Jack Joseph Puig. Controls: Body (low end), Presence (mid-high), Air (very top end), Compress, Reverb, Delay, Effects. Character: upfront, present, exciting vocal sound — JJP's signature vocal treatment from countless rock hits. Choose for quick professional vocal processing. Best for: rock/pop/punk vocals, lead vocals needing to cut through, aggressive vocal styles.

name: Kaleidoscopes
description: Creative multi-effect processor with two independent modulation engines that generate ever-changing patterns. Each engine: phaser, flanger, chorus, tremolo, all with randomization and pattern generation. Controls: Speed, Depth, Feedback, Waveform, Randomize, Sync. Character: constantly evolving, unpredictable, organic modulation textures. Choose over standard chorus/flanger when you want evolving, never-repeating modulation. Best for: ambient textures, synth pads, guitar shimmer, creating evolving soundscapes, psychedelic effects.

name: Key Detector
description: Automatic musical key and chord detection in real-time. Displays detected root note and scale (major/minor/modes). Also shows chord progressions. ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY — does not process audio. Best for: determining the key of a song for pitch correction setup, DJ mixing (harmonic mixing), music production reference.

name: Kramer HLS
description: Modeled Helios Type 69 console EQ by Eddie Kramer — the EQ sound of Led Zeppelin, Hendrix, and Olympic Studios. 3 bands: Bass (shelf, 60/120Hz), Mid (parametric, 0.7-7kHz), Treble (shelf, 10/12/16kHz). Character: warm, smooth, richly colored — adds vintage British console magic. Very musical, nothing like modern clean EQ. Choose over modern EQs when you want heavy vintage coloration. Best for: drums (the Bonham sound), guitars (the Hendrix tone), vocals (classic rock warmth), anything needing vintage British console character.

name: Kramer PIE
description: Modeled PIE (Pye) compressor/limiter used at Olympic Studios. Simple controls: Input, Output, Recovery (release), Limit/Compress mode. Character: gentle, program-dependent compression with vintage smoothness. Very subtle, flattering compression. Choose over aggressive compressors when you want barely-there vintage limiting. Best for: gentle bus compression, mastering (subtle limiting), vocals needing transparent control, any source where compression should be invisible.

name: Kramer Tape
description: Analog tape machine emulation. Controls: Tape Speed (7.5/15/30 IPS), Record Level (into saturation), Tape Type, Wow/Flutter (depth + rate), Noise, Bias, HF/LF adjustment, Delay (for slapback). Character: warmth, gentle compression, HF smoothing, subtle pitch wobble, harmonic saturation. Lower speeds = more color, higher = cleaner. Choose over J37 when you want simpler tape emulation with less historical specificity. Best for: mix bus (adds analog warmth to digital mixes), drums, vocals, guitars — any source needing tape warmth. One of the most-used saturation plugins.

name: L1 limiter
description: First-generation Waves brick-wall peak limiter. Controls: Threshold, Release, Output Ceiling, and IDR dithering for bit-depth reduction. Character: effective but slightly aggressive at heavy limiting. Choose L2 or newer limiters for transparent results; L1 adds more character/color. Best for: utility peak limiting, dithering for bit-depth conversion, situations where slight limiter coloration is desired, vintage Waves limiter sound.

name: L1+ Ultramaximizer
description: Enhanced L1 with automatic gain optimization and improved dithering algorithms. Same basic limiter engine as L1 with better metering and auto-makeup gain. Choose over L1 for improved workflow. Best for: same as L1 with better ergonomics.

name: L2
description: Second-generation brick-wall limiter with ARC (Auto Release Control) — intelligent release timing that adapts to program material for transparent limiting. Controls: Threshold, Output Ceiling, ARC on/off, IDR dithering with noise shaping options. Character: transparent, professional, industry-standard. ARC is the key feature — prevents pumping by automatically adjusting release time. Choose over L1 for transparency. Choose over L316 for simpler workflow. Best for: mastering (industry standard final limiter), dithering for delivery, any situation needing transparent loudness maximization without artifacts.

name: L2-SC
description: L2 limiter with sidechain filtering. Adds HPF/LPF filters on the sidechain detector so bass-heavy material doesn't trigger excessive limiting. Choose over standard L2 when bass is causing pumping/distortion during limiting. Best for: mastering bass-heavy genres (EDM, hip-hop), any material where low-frequency energy causes problematic limiter behavior.

name: L3 MultiMaximizer
description: 5-band multiband brick-wall limiter. Each band has independent threshold and priority controls. Limits each frequency band independently for more transparent loudness with preserved spectral balance. Controls: per-band threshold, Priority, Release, Profile (presets for different material types). Character: louder and more transparent than single-band limiting. Choose over L2 when you need louder masters without spectral distortion. Best for: mastering (especially competitive loudness), broadcast, EDM/pop mastering where loudness matters, material with wide dynamic range across spectrum.

name: L3 UltraMaximizer
description: Single-band version of L3 with same quality processing but simplified to one band. Controls: Threshold, Ceiling, Profile, Release. Character: excellent quality single-band limiting with L3 engine. Choose over L2 when you want L3-quality limiting without multiband complexity. Best for: simpler mastering tasks, quick loudness maximization with L3 quality.

name: L3-LL Multi
description: Low-latency version of L3 MultiMaximizer for live applications. Same 5-band multiband limiting with minimal processing delay. Choose over studio L3 for live use. Best for: live broadcast, live mastering, real-time loudness management.

name: L3-LL Ultra
description: Low-latency version of L3 UltraMaximizer. Single-band L3 limiting with minimal delay. Best for: live sound, live broadcast, real-time peak limiting.

name: L316
description: Mastering limiter combining multiband processing with harmonic enhancement. Unique approach: adds subtle saturation alongside limiting for louder, fuller-sounding masters. Controls: Threshold, Ceiling, Analog Trim (saturation amount), Priority, Release. Character: loud AND warm — the saturation prevents the 'thin squashed' sound of pure limiting. Choose over L2/L3 when you want loud masters that still sound full and warm. Best for: modern mastering (competitive loudness with warmth), EDM, pop, hip-hop, rock — any genre where loudness AND fullness matter.

name: L4 Ultramaximizer
description: Latest generation brick-wall limiter with the most advanced ARC (Auto Release Control) technology. Improved algorithm over L2 for even more transparent limiting at extreme settings. Controls: Threshold, Ceiling, ARC, IDR dithering. Character: the most transparent Waves limiter — handles extreme gain reduction better than predecessors. Choose over L2 when you need to push loudness harder without artifacts. Best for: demanding mastering situations, very dynamic material, pushing loudness while maintaining quality.

name: LinEQ Broadband
description: Linear-phase broadband EQ for mastering. 5 bands of parametric EQ with zero phase distortion across the full spectrum. Controls: standard parametric per band (Freq, Gain, Q) plus HP/LP filters. Character: utterly transparent — EQ changes happen without any phase shift, preserving transient shape and stereo image. Choose over minimum-phase EQs (H-EQ, etc.) when phase accuracy matters (mastering). Best for: mastering (the go-to EQ type for mastering), critical listening applications, any EQ application where preserving phase relationships is essential.

name: LinEQ Lowband
description: Linear-phase low-frequency EQ focused on bass and sub-bass. Precision low-end equalization without phase shift. Character: transparent bass EQ — especially important in low frequencies where phase shift from conventional EQ causes the most damage. Choose when you need to EQ bass without the phase issues that conventional EQ causes in low frequencies. Best for: mastering low-end adjustments, bass-heavy music, EDM/hip-hop sub-bass management.

name: LinMB
description: Linear-phase multiband compressor with 5 bands and zero phase distortion. Controls per band: Threshold, Range (amount), Attack, Release, Gain. Master: Adaptive Release, Mix. Character: transparent multiband dynamics without the phase issues of conventional multiband processors. Choose over C4/C6 when phase accuracy matters (mastering). Best for: mastering (the premium multiband compressor for mastering), critical bus processing, any multiband dynamics task where phase integrity is essential.

name: LoAir
description: Sub-bass enhancement generator using harmonic synthesis. Creates sub-harmonics below the fundamental frequency to add weight and depth. Controls: Amount, Lo/Hi alignment, Mix. Character: adds deep, powerful sub-bass rumble that you feel rather than hear. Choose over EQ bass boost when there's no sub content to boost (LoAir generates new sub content). Best for: kick drums (adding sub weight), bass (extending into sub range), full mix sub-bass enhancement, EDM/hip-hop sub-bass reinforcement, any audio lacking sub-bass content.

name: Lofi Space
description: Lo-fi delay and reverb combination with vintage degradation character. Sections: Delay (with lo-fi degradation, filtering), Reverb (with vintage character), combined output. name: MDMX Screamer

name: MV2
description: Dual-action dynamics plugin that simultaneously controls BOTH peaks AND quiet parts. Best for: vocals (evening out wildly dynamic performance), dialogue, acoustic instruments, podcasts — anything with too much dynamic range that needs leveling from both ends.

name: Magma BB Tubes

name: Magma Channel Strip

name: Magma Lil Tube

Choose when you want fast tube saturation without deep parameter diving. name: Magma Springs

name: MannyM Reverb

name: MannyM Tone Shaper
description: Multiband tone-shaping processor by Manny Marroquin. Combines frequency-selective dynamics with tonal control for spectral shaping. Controls per band: shape amount, character.
