name: MannyM TripleD
description: Triple problem-solver: De-Esser + De-Harsher + De-Boxer by Manny Marroquin. Three independent processors targeting sibilance (4-10kHz harshness), harshness (2-4kHz), and boxiness (200-600Hz). Each section has its own controls. Character: targeted problem-solving without affecting good frequencies. Choose when vocals have multiple frequency problems simultaneously. Best for: vocals with sibilance + harshness + boxiness issues, dialogue cleanup, any source with multiple frequency-domain problems.

name: Maserati ACG
description: Acoustic guitar processor by Tony Maserati (Beyoncé, Jay-Z, Alicia Keys). Controls: Body (low-end fullness), Edge (presence/attack), Compress, Ambience. Character: polished, clear, present acoustic guitar. Choose for quick professional acoustic guitar processing. Best for: acoustic guitar in pop/R&B, singer-songwriter productions, any acoustic guitar needing professional polish.

name: Maserati B72
description: Bass processor by Tony Maserati. Controls: Sub (sub-bass), Punch (mid-bass attack), Grind (distortion), Compress, Ambience. Character: full, punchy, modern bass. Choose for quick professional bass processing. Best for: bass guitar in pop/R&B/hip-hop, synth bass, modern bass production.

name: Maserati DRM
description: Drum processor by Tony Maserati. Separate controls for different drum characteristics: Attack, Body, Room, Compression. Character: polished, punchy, modern drum sound — Tony Maserati's signature drum treatment. Choose for quick professional drum processing. Best for: drum bus in pop/R&B, modern drum production, drums needing polished contemporary treatment.

name: Maserati GRP
description: Master bus processor by Tony Maserati. Complete mix bus chain: stereo enhancement, compression, EQ, limiting. Character: polished, wide, modern — Tony Maserati's mix finalization approach. Choose for modern pop/R&B mix bus processing. Best for: mix bus in pop/R&B productions, master bus sweetening, quick mix finalization.

name: Maserati GTi
description: Electric guitar processor by Tony Maserati. Controls: Bite (presence), Body (fullness), Compress, Ambience. Character: polished, modern electric guitar sound. Choose for electric guitar in pop/R&B context. Best for: electric guitar in modern pop/R&B, clean to light drive guitar tones, guitar needing polished contemporary treatment.

name: Maserati HMX
description: Harmonic enhancer by Tony Maserati. Adds presence, sparkle, and harmonic richness through multiband harmonic generation. Character: exciting, bright, present — adds life and energy. Choose for quick harmonic enhancement. Best for: drums (adding excitement), vocals (presence), mix bus (sparkle), any source needing energy and harmonic enhancement.

name: Maserati VX1
description: Vocal processor by Tony Maserati. Complete vocal chain: compression, EQ, de-essing, doubling, reverb, delay. Character: polished, modern, radio-ready — Tony Maserati's vocal treatment for major pop/R&B/hip-hop releases. Choose for modern pop/R&B vocal production. Best for: pop/R&B/hip-hop vocals, lead vocal processing, background vocal bus.

name: MaxxBass
description: Sub-bass enhancement using psychoacoustic bass synthesis. Generates upper harmonics of bass frequencies that trick the ear into perceiving bass on speakers too small to reproduce it. Controls: Original Bass, MaxxBass (harmonic amount), Frequency (crossover), Response (decay). Character: makes bass translate on ALL speakers — from laptop to club. Choose over LoAir when translation across playback systems is the goal (LoAir adds real sub, MaxxBass adds perceived bass). Best for: ensuring bass translates on headphones/laptops/phones, pop/rock mastering, bass guitar, any bass-heavy content that must work on small speakers.

name: MaxxVolume
description: Multi-stage dynamics combining Gate + Leveler + Compressor + Limiter in one plugin. Each stage processes sequentially: gate removes noise, leveler evens out long-term dynamics, compressor controls short-term dynamics, limiter prevents peaks. Controls per stage: threshold, amount, speed. Character: comprehensive dynamics control — handles everything from noise to peaks. Choose when you need complete dynamics management in one plugin. Best for: wildly dynamic vocals (radio/podcast), dialogue, live recordings with noise + dynamics issues, any source needing gate + comp + limiter in one chain.

name: MetaFilter
description: Creative multi-mode resonant filter with advanced modulation. Filter types: LP, HP, BP, Notch, Comb. Modulation sources: LFO (multiple shapes), Envelope Follower, Step Sequencer. Controls: Cutoff, Resonance, Modulation source select, Rate, Depth, Sync. Character: from subtle movement to extreme filter sweeps — the most creative filter available. Choose for creative filter effects (not utility filtering). Best for: synths (classic filter sweeps), EDM builds/drops, guitar filter effects, DJ-style filter transitions, sound design, creative vocal effects.

name: MetaFlanger
description: Advanced flanging effect with analog tape flanging simulation. Controls: Rate, Depth, Feedback, Manual (center frequency), Tape/Electric mode, Stereo spread. Tape mode simulates real tape flanging (two machines). Character: from subtle motion to jet-engine flanging sweeps. Choose when you specifically want flanging (not chorus or phasing). Best for: guitars (classic flanger), synths, drums, vocal effects, creating the iconic 'jet swoosh' flanging effect.

name: MondoMod
description: Combined modulation effects: AM (amplitude modulation/tremolo), FM (frequency modulation/vibrato), and Rotation (rotary speaker simulation). Each section has Rate, Depth, and Waveform controls with tempo sync. Character: classic modulation effects — tremolo for pulsating volume, vibrato for pitch wobble, rotation for Leslie speaker simulation. Choose when you want tremolo, vibrato, or rotary effects. Best for: guitar (tremolo, Leslie), organ (rotary speaker), synths (vibrato), creative vocal effects.

name: Morphoder
description: 10-band vocoder/talk box effect. Analyzes one signal (carrier) and imposes its spectral shape on another (modulator), or uses built-in synth as carrier. Controls: Carrier select, Modulator input, Filter Q, Noise amount, built-in synth settings. Character: robotic vocals, talking instruments — classic vocoder/talk box sounds. Choose for vocoder/talk box effects specifically. Best for: robotic vocal effects, talk box sounds, synth vocoding, creative cross-synthesis between any two sources.

name: MultiMod Rack
description: Multi-effects modulation rack with multiple chainable effect slots. Available effects: Chorus, Flanger, Phaser, Tremolo, Vibrato, Rotary. Can chain multiple modulation effects in series. Character: complex combined modulation effects. Choose when you need multiple modulation effects chained together. Best for: complex modulation chains, creative effects, ambient guitar rigs, synth processing.

name: NLS Buss
description: Non-Linear Summer BUS channel — analog mix bus summing emulation. Models three different console mix buses: Spike (Neve 5116 — warm, wide), Mike (SSL 4000E — tight, punchy), Nevo (EMI TG12345 — rich, harmonic). Controls: Bus model, Drive, Trim. Character: adds the subtle nonlinear distortion and coloration of analog mix bus summing. Choose when you want analog summing character on your mix bus. Best for: mix bus (primary use), submix buses, adding analog console depth to digital summing.

name: NLS Channel
description: Non-Linear Summer CHANNEL strip — analog channel emulation with per-channel variation. Same three console models as NLS Buss but each instance gets a slightly different channel (like real consoles where every channel sounds slightly different). Controls: Console model, Channel variation, Drive, Trim. Character: subtle per-channel variation adding depth and 3D quality. Choose when you want each track in your mix to sound slightly different (like a real console). Best for: use on every channel in a mix for realistic analog console variation, adding depth and separation between tracks.

name: NS1
description: One-knob noise suppressor using real-time spectral analysis. Single control: Amount (noise reduction intensity). Automatically identifies and separates noise from signal — no noise profile capture needed. Character: transparent, simple, effective — just turn the knob until noise disappears. Choose over X-Noise/Z-Noise when you want the fastest possible noise reduction workflow. Best for: quick noise cleanup on vocals, dialogue, podcasts, live recordings — any scenario where you need fast noise reduction without parameter diving.

name: NX
description: Headphone monitoring plugin using Waves Nx 3D audio technology with head tracking. Simulates the experience of listening on speakers in a treated room while wearing headphones. Tracks head movement for realistic spatial perception. MONITORING TOOL — does not process audio for the mix. Best for: mixing on headphones when speakers aren't available, checking stereo image accuracy on headphones.

name: NX Ambisonics
description: Ambisonics monitoring on headphones with Nx head-tracking technology. Monitors B-Format ambisonics content through headphones with realistic 3D spatial perception. For VR/immersive audio monitoring. Not relevant for standard stereo mixing.

name: Nx Ambisonics
description: Variant of NX Ambisonics headphone monitoring. Same spatial audio technology for ambisonics monitoring on headphones. For VR/immersive audio production.

name: Nx Germano Studios
description: Headphone monitoring simulating the control room of Germano Studios NYC. Nx technology recreating a specific legendary studio environment. MONITORING TOOL. Best for: mixing on headphones with a specific studio reference.

name: Nx Ocean Way Nashville
description: Headphone monitoring simulating Ocean Way Nashville studio control room. Nx technology for accurate spatial monitoring. MONITORING TOOL. Best for: mixing on headphones with a Nashville studio reference.

name: OVox
description: Advanced voice-controlled synthesizer and vocal effects processor. Features: voice-to-synth (plays synth with your voice), vocoder, talkbox, harmonizer, auto-tune, 8 FX modules, MIDI integration. Controls: Source (voice input), Synth engine, FX chain, MIDI settings, Voicing. Character: from subtle harmonizing to extreme vocal transformation — the most powerful vocal effects processor available. Choose for creative vocal effects beyond simple processing. Best for: vocal sound design, electronic vocal effects, EDM vocal production, creative harmonizing, robotic/alien voice effects, synth-vocal hybrid sounds.

name: OneKnob Brighter
description: Single-knob high-frequency enhancer. One dial from 0 (no change) to 10 (maximum brightness). Applies intelligent high-frequency enhancement curve. Character: quick brightness boost without harshness. Choose when you want the fastest possible brightening. Best for: quick brightening of dull recordings, adding top-end sparkle with minimal effort, sessions needing rapid tonal fixes.

name: OneKnob Driver
description: Single-knob saturation and drive. One dial from 0 (clean) to 10 (heavy distortion). Progressive saturation from subtle warmth to aggressive overdrive. Character: increasingly aggressive harmonic drive. Choose for fastest-possible saturation workflow. Best for: quick warmth/drive on any source, adding character with one dial, rapid tonal enhancement.

name: OneKnob Filter
description: Single-knob resonant filter sweep. One dial sweeps from full low-pass (dark) through open to full high-pass (thin). Resonance at filter point. Character: DJ-style filter sweeps. Best for: DJ transitions, build-ups/drops, creative filter effects, automation.

name: OneKnob Louder
description: Single-knob loudness maximizer. One dial from 0 (unity) to 10 (maximum loudness). Intelligent limiting and gain optimization. Character: progressive loudness increase. Best for: quick loudness boost, demos, rough mixes needing quick volume, podcasts.

name: OneKnob Phatter
description: Single-knob low-frequency enhancer. One dial from 0 (no change) to 10 (maximum bass enhancement). Adds low-frequency warmth and weight. Character: quick bass boost. Best for: thin recordings needing bass, drums needing weight, quick low-end enhancement.

name: OneKnob Pressure
description: Single-knob compressor. One dial from 0 (no compression) to 10 (heavy squash). Progressive compression from gentle to extreme. Character: increasingly obvious compression from subtle to pumping. Best for: quick compression on any source, parallel compression (mix knob), rapid dynamics control.

name: OneKnob Pumper
description: Single-knob rhythmic ducking/pumping effect. Creates sidechain-style volume pumping synchronized to tempo WITHOUT needing an external sidechain trigger. One dial controls pump depth. Character: classic EDM sidechain pumping. Best for: EDM production (sidechain effect without routing), rhythmic pumping on pads/synths/bass, dance music production, adding rhythmic motion to static elements.

name: OneKnob Wetter
description: Single-knob reverb. One dial from 0 (dry) to 10 (maximum reverb). Character: simple room reverb. Best for: quick ambience on any source, adding room feel with minimal effort.

name: PAZ- Analyzer
description: Comprehensive audio analysis suite: real-time frequency spectrum, stereo field display (Lissajous), peak/RMS meters. Multiple display modes and resolution settings. ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY — no audio processing. Best for: frequency analysis during mixing, stereo imaging verification, level monitoring, identifying problem frequencies visually.

name: PAZ- Frequency
description: Real-time frequency spectrum analyzer. Displays frequency content with adjustable FFT resolution, averaging, and peak hold. ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY. Best for: identifying frequency buildups, checking spectral balance, finding problematic resonances visually.

name: PAZ- Meters
description: Peak and RMS level metering. Multiple meter scales (VU, PPM, digital). Displays both peak and average simultaneously. ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY. Best for: level monitoring during mixing and mastering.

name: PAZ- Position
description: Stereo field position analyzer showing the stereo image as a vectorscope/Lissajous display. Visualizes width, balance, and mono compatibility. ANALYSIS TOOL ONLY. Best for: checking stereo width and balance, verifying mono compatibility, identifying stereo imaging problems.

name: PRS Archon
description: Modeled PRS Archon guitar amplifier. High-gain amp with tight low-end and aggressive modern voicing. Controls: Gain, Volume, Bass, Mid, Treble, Presence, Bright switch, Cabinet select. Character: tight, aggressive, modern high-gain — designed for heavy rock and metal. Choose when you need high-gain metal/djent tones. Best for: metal guitar, hard rock, djent, progressive metal, any heavy guitar style needing tight articulation at high gain.

name: PRS Dallas
description: Modeled PRS Dallas guitar amplifier. Vintage-voiced amp with warm overdrive character. Controls: Gain, Volume, Bass, Mid, Treble, Cabinet select. Character: warm, vintage, classic — American clean to mid-gain overdrive. Choose for blues, classic rock, roots tones. Best for: blues guitar, classic rock, country, roots, clean-to-crunch tones.

name: PRS V9
description: Modeled PRS V9 guitar amplifier. Versatile amp covering clean through high-gain. Controls: Gain, Volume, Bass, Mid, Treble, Bright switch, Cabinet select, Channel select. Character: wide-ranging — from clean sparkle through crunch to high-gain. Choose when you need one amp that covers multiple gain ranges. Best for: versatile guitar sessions, recording multiple styles, sessions needing clean + dirty tones from one amp.

name: PS22 Split
description: Stereo split: separates audio into low and high frequencies, then pans them to different stereo positions. Controls: Crossover frequency, spread amount. Character: frequency-dependent stereo widening. Choose for creative stereo effects based on frequency separation. Best for: creating stereo width from mono by splitting frequencies, creative stereo effects, widening bass or treble independently.

name: PS22 Spread
description: Stereo spreading using micro pitch-shifting. Creates stereo width by slightly pitch-shifting left and right channels in opposite directions. Controls: Spread amount, Frequency range. Character: effective stereo widening that works on any mono source. Choose over S1 Imager when the source is mono and needs stereo width (S1 works on existing stereo). Best for: mono-to-stereo widening, thickening vocals/guitars/synths, adding width to narrow recordings.

name: PS22 Spread(10)
description: Extended 10-voice version of PS22 Spread for richer stereo spreading. Uses 10 pitch-shifted voices instead of standard 2 for much thicker, more complex stereo image. Choose over PS22 Spread when you want maximum thickness and width. Best for: creating very wide stereo from mono, thick vocal stacks, lush pad widening, maximum stereo enhancement.

name: PS22 XSplit
description: Advanced stereo split with adjustable crossover and precise frequency-dependent panning control. More control than PS22 Split with adjustable crossover slope and wider parameter range. Choose over PS22 Split for more precise frequency-based stereo manipulation. Best for: detailed frequency-dependent stereo work, creative stereo design, mastering width adjustments.

name: PSE
description: Peak Spectrum Expander for dynamic spectral enhancement. Detects and enhances spectral peaks to add presence and clarity. Controls: Amount, Range, Speed. Character: subtle presence enhancement — makes audio sound more alive and detailed. Choose when standard EQ boosting sounds harsh but audio needs more presence. Best for: dull or lifeless recordings, adding subtle presence without EQ, enhancing detail in dense mixes.

name: PlaylistRider
description: Automatic gain rider for mastering playlists and compilations. Maintains consistent loudness across multiple tracks with different levels. Controls: Target level, Speed, Range. Character: transparent level matching. Choose for album/playlist level consistency. Best for: mastering engineers (matching track levels across an album), playlist creation, compilation mastering, podcast level consistency.

name: PuigChild 660
description: Modeled Fairchild 660 MONO tube compressor by Jack Joseph Puig. The Fairchild 660/670 is the most coveted and expensive vintage compressor ever made (originals sell for $30K-50K+). 20 tubes, transformer-coupled, program-dependent timing with 6 time constants. Controls: Input Gain, Threshold, Time Constant (1-6, from fast to slow), Output Gain. Character: incredibly smooth, warm, thick tube compression with rich harmonic saturation. The compression 'breathes' musically. Choose over any other compressor when you want the ultimate vintage warmth and musicality. Best for: vocals (legendary vocal compressor), bus compression (gentle glue with tube warmth), mastering (the ultimate gentle touch).

name: PuigChild 670
description: Modeled Fairchild 670 STEREO tube compressor by Jack Joseph Puig. Stereo version of the 660 with linked or independent channel control. Same legendary tube circuit with 20+ tubes. Controls: Input, Threshold, Time Constant (1-6), Output, L/R link. Character: same incredible smoothness and warmth as 660 but in stereo — legendary on mix bus and mastering. Choose over SSLComp when you want warm, tube-colored bus compression vs clean VCA glue. Best for: mix bus (the ultimate warm bus compressor), stereo mastering, stereo submix processing, anything needing gentle, warm stereo compression.

name: PuigTec EQP1A
description: Modeled Pultec EQP-1A passive tube EQ — perhaps the most revered EQ in recording history. Unique design: separate Boost AND Attenuate controls at the SAME bass frequency (the famous 'Pultec trick' — boosting and cutting simultaneously creates a unique resonant low-end shape). Bands: Low (20-100Hz boost+atten), High Boost (3-16kHz with bandwidth), High Atten (shelf). Character: silky, smooth, impossibly musical — adds tube warmth and harmonic beauty. The high boost is 'airy' not 'harsh'. Choose when you want the most musical EQ possible. Best for: bass sweetening (the Pultec bass trick is legendary), adding air to vocals, kick drum low-end shaping, mix bus sweetening, mastering — anywhere you need beautiful EQ.

name: PuigTec MEQ5
description: Modeled Pultec MEQ-5 passive tube midrange EQ — the companion to the EQP-1A covering midrange. Two Mid bands: Low-Mid peak (200-1000Hz) and High-Mid dip (1.5-5kHz), plus separate High boost (3-12kHz). Character: same silky, smooth Pultec character as EQP-1A but focused on midrange. The mid dip is legendary for clearing vocal mud. Together with EQP-1A covers the full spectrum. Best for: vocals (clearing 1-3kHz mud while adding presence), guitars, piano, any midrange-heavy source. Essential companion to EQP-1A for full Pultec treatment.

name: Q-Capture
description: EQ curve capture tool — records the frequency response of an external hardware EQ for use with Q-Clone. Part of the Q-Clone EQ matching system. Insert on a hardware send/return to capture the hardware EQ's curve. UTILITY TOOL for Q-Clone workflow. Best for: capturing hardware EQ responses for digital recall.

name: Q-Clone
description: EQ cloning plugin that applies frequency curves captured by Q-Capture. Replicates the exact frequency response of any external hardware EQ in real-time. Character: matches whatever hardware it's cloning. Choose when you want to use expensive hardware EQ on many tracks without multiple hardware units. Best for: applying hardware EQ to multiple tracks, hardware EQ recall, hybrid analog/digital workflows.

name: Q1
description: 1-band parametric EQ. Single fully parametric band with Frequency, Gain, Q controls plus filter type (bell/shelf/cut). Minimal CPU. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: single targeted frequency adjustment with absolute minimum CPU, utility EQ, simple corrections.

name: Q10
description: 10-band parametric EQ — the most bands available in a Waves parametric EQ. Ten fully parametric bands for maximum detail. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: extremely detailed EQ work, situations needing many simultaneous corrections, complex tonal reconstruction.

name: Q2
description: 2-band parametric EQ. Two fully parametric bands. Minimal CPU. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: simple 2-point corrections with minimum CPU overhead.

name: Q3
description: 3-band parametric EQ. Three fully parametric bands. Efficient processing. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: basic tonal shaping with 3 bands, moderate EQ tasks with low CPU.

name: Q4
description: 4-band parametric EQ. Four fully parametric bands — sufficient for most EQ tasks. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: general-purpose mixing EQ, standard tonal corrections, when you need solid EQ without extra features.

name: Q6

name: Q8
description: 8-band parametric EQ. Eight fully parametric bands for surgical work. Character: clean, transparent. Best for: very detailed EQ work, mastering-level frequency sculpting, complex tonal problems needing many correction points.

name: RBass
description: Renaissance Bass — low-frequency enhancement using harmonic synthesis. Generates harmonics of bass frequencies to create perceived bass that translates across all playback systems. Controls: Intensity (harmonic amount), Frequency (crossover — below this gets harmonics), Original (dry bass level). Character: warm, present bass that works on any speaker. Different from LoAir (which generates sub-harmonics below the fundamental) — RBass generates UPPER harmonics for perceived bass. Best for: bass guitar (essential for translation), kick drum, any bass source that must translate on small speakers/headphones/phones, pop/rock bass enhancement.

name: RChannel
description: Renaissance Channel strip combining 4-band EQ, compressor, gate, and limiter with warm analog-modeled character. EQ: 2 parametric mids, HF/LF shelving with HPF/LPF. Compressor: threshold/ratio/attack/release with Opto/Electro modes. Gate: threshold/floor/attack/release. Character: warm, musical — the Renaissance series adds subtle analog warmth. Choose when you want a complete channel strip with warm character. Best for: general-purpose channel processing on any source, vocal chains, drum channels, one-plugin channel processing.

name: RCompressor
description: Renaissance Compressor with analog-modeled warmth. Controls: Threshold, Ratio, Attack (0.005-500ms), Release (1-5000ms), Gain, ARC (Auto Release), Opto/Electro mode. Opto mode: smooth, program-dependent (like an optical compressor). Electro mode: faster, more precise (like VCA). Character: warm, musical, versatile — one of the most-used compressors for its balance of control and musicality. Choose when you want warm, easy compression without deep parameter diving. Best for: any source — vocals, drums, bass, guitars, bus. The jack-of-all-trades compressor.

name: RDeEsser
description: Renaissance De-Esser with natural-sounding sibilance control. Split-band processing targets only the sibilant frequencies. Controls: Threshold, Frequency (sibilance target), Attenuation range, Monitor mode. Character: smooth, natural de-essing that preserves vocal air while reducing harshness. Choose over standard DeEsser for more natural results. Choose Sibilance for the most transparent/modern approach. Best for: vocals with sibilance, podcast de-essing, any vocal needing sibilance control with natural results.

name: REQ 2
description: Renaissance EQ with 2 bands. Warm, analog-modeled parametric EQ. Character: musical, warm — adds subtle Renaissance-series analog flavor. Best for: simple corrections with warm character, situations needing minimal EQ with analog warmth.

name: REQ 4
description: Renaissance EQ with 4 bands. Warm, analog-modeled parametric EQ with four fully parametric bands plus HP/LP filters. Character: warm, musical — balance between transparency and analog character. Choose when you want musical EQ with 4 bands. Best for: mixing EQ with warm character, vocals, guitars, drums — versatile musical equalization.

name: REQ 6
description: Renaissance EQ with 6 bands. The most complete Renaissance EQ with six parametric bands. Character: same warm Renaissance sound with comprehensive band count. Best for: detailed EQ work wanting warm analog character, comprehensive tonal shaping with musicality.

name: RVerb
description: Renaissance Reverb — versatile algorithmic reverb with multiple room types. Types: Hall, Room, Plate, Chamber, Church, Inverse, Gated, Non-Linear. Controls: Time, Size, Diffusion, Density, Damping, Pre-Delay, EQ, Early Reflections, Mix. Character: warm, musical, versatile — covers many reverb styles in one plugin. Choose as an all-purpose reverb when you don't need the premium quality of H-Reverb. Best for: general-purpose reverb on any source, utility reverb, gated/non-linear effects, creative reverb with good variety.

name: RVox
description: Renaissance Vox — vocal compressor/gate designed specifically for voice. Ultra-simple: Threshold, Gain, Gate controls (that's it). Automatic attack/release timing optimized for vocal dynamics. Built-in gate removes noise between phrases. Character: warm, simple, effective — the fastest way to compress a vocal. Choose when you want vocal compression with absolute minimum fuss. Best for: vocals (the fastest vocal compressor to set up), podcasts, dialogue, voiceover — any voice recording needing quick compression.

name: Renaissance Axx
description: Guitar/bass compressor with program-dependent behavior optimized for string instruments. Controls: Threshold, Gain, Attack, Release. Character: smooth, musical compression that responds well to the dynamics of plucked strings. Choose over general compressors when processing guitar or bass specifically. Best for: acoustic guitar, electric guitar (clean), bass guitar, any plucked string instrument.

name: Retro Fi
description: Comprehensive vintage lo-fi multi-effect with 6 sections: Device (tape/vinyl/radio degradation), Space (reverb), Reverb (separate from space), Echo (delay), Noise (hiss/crackle/hum), and mechanical degradation. Each section independently on/off with detailed controls. Device Mix control is critical — don't set to 100% or you lose all clarity. Character: authentic retro degradation — makes anything sound like it's from another era. Choose when you want comprehensive vintage/lo-fi treatment. Best for: lo-fi hip-hop, vaporwave, vintage aesthetics, tape/vinyl/radio simulation, creating nostalgic textures. IMPORTANT: Set Device Mix to 20-40% not 100%.

name: S1 Imager
description: Stereo imaging tool for adjusting the width of existing stereo signals. Controls: Width (from mono through original to ultra-wide), Rotation, Asymmetry, Shuffling (bass narrowing). Visual stereo display. Character: transparent stereo manipulation. Choose for adjusting existing stereo width. Choose PS22 Spread for making mono sources stereo (S1 only works on existing stereo). Best for: narrowing too-wide mixes, widening narrow mixes, bass mono-ification for vinyl/club, mastering stereo adjustments, checking mono compatibility.

name: S1 MS Matrix
description: Mid-Side encoder/decoder for stereo manipulation. Converts L/R stereo to Mid+Side and back, allowing independent processing of center (Mid) and side (Side) content. Character: transparent M/S conversion utility. Best for: M/S processing workflows (insert EQ/compression between encoder and decoder), creative stereo manipulation, mastering M/S techniques, independent processing of center vs side content.

name: S1 Shuffler
description: Advanced stereo processor with frequency-dependent width control and bass mono-ification. Controls: Shuffling (frequency-dependent width), Width, Bass Frequency (below this = mono), Rotation. Character: precise stereo sculpting. Choose over S1 Imager when you need frequency-dependent width control (narrow the bass, widen the highs). Best for: mastering (frequency-dependent stereo control), bass mono-ification for vinyl/club, stereo optimization, making mixes wider in highs and tighter in lows.

name: SSL EV2 Channel
description: Modeled SSL E-Series V2 channel strip — the updated version of the most famous recording console in history. Sections: Preamp (with analog modeling), HPF/LPF Filters (12/18dB slopes), 4-band EQ (HF/HMF/LMF/LF with parametric mids and shelving highs/lows), Dynamics (compressor with ratio/threshold/attack/release PLUS expander/gate), Channel Mode switch (Cut/Boost). Character: clean, punchy, detailed — THE sound of modern music. Choose when you want complete channel processing with SSL precision. Best for: literally everything — vocals, drums, bass, guitars, keys, bus. The most versatile channel strip ever made.

name: SSLChannel
description: Modeled SSL E-Series channel strip (original version). Sections: HPF/LPF, 4-band EQ (same topology as SSL EV2 but original modeling), Dynamics (comp + gate/expander). Character: punchy, detailed, slightly more 'vintage' than the EV2. Choose over EV2 when you want the original SSL sound. Best for: same as EV2 — works on everything. Industry-standard channel processing.

name: SSLComp
description: Modeled SSL G-Series stereo bus compressor — THE most famous mix bus compressor in history, found on virtually every SSL console. Controls: Threshold, Ratio (2/4/10:1), Attack (0.1/0.3/1/3/10/30ms), Release (0.1/0.3/0.6/1.2s + Auto), Makeup Gain. Character: tight, punchy, gluing — makes a mix feel cohesive and powerful. The Auto release is legendary for mix bus use. Choose over Fairchild/PuigChild when you want modern punch vs vintage warmth. Choose over API-2500 for tighter, less aggressive glue. Best for: mix bus (THE primary use — put it on your mix bus and everything glues together), drum bus, group buses, any bus needing cohesion. Ratio 2:1 or 4:1, Auto release for mix bus.

name: SSLEQ
description: Modeled SSL E-Series parametric EQ. Same EQ section as the SSLChannel but standalone. 4 bands: HF shelf, HMF parametric, LMF parametric, LF shelf. HPF included. Character: punchy, musical, detailed — the SSL EQ sound. Choose when you want just the SSL EQ without the dynamics section. Best for: mixing EQ on any source, achieving SSL console tone, punchy tonal shaping.

name: SSLGChannel
description: Modeled SSL G-Series channel strip. The G-Series is a different SSL console from the E-Series — slightly different character. Sections: 4-band EQ, Dynamics (comp + gate). Character: clean, precise, slightly less 'punchy' than E-Series and more refined. Choose over E-Series when you want a slightly smoother, more refined SSL sound. Best for: vocals, acoustic instruments, mastering applications, any source needing refined SSL processing.

name: Saphira
description: Harmonic enhancer with multiple harmonic generation algorithms. Offers different harmonic profiles: Warm, Bright, Round, Dirty, and more. Controls: Intensity, Harmonic profile select, Mix, Output. Character: versatile saturation/enhancement — from subtle warmth to heavy harmonic coloring depending on profile. Choose over single-type saturation plugins when you want to explore different harmonic characters. Best for: vocals, drums, bus, mastering — anywhere harmonics can enhance the source. Good for A/B comparing different saturation types.

name: Scheps 73
description: Modeled Neve 1073 EQ by mix legend Andrew Scheps. 3 bands: LF shelf (35-220Hz), Mid peak (360Hz-7.2kHz), HF shelf (12kHz fixed). HPF (50-300Hz). The 1073 is arguably the most iconic console EQ ever made — found on every major studio's Neve consoles. Character: huge, warm, musical, larger-than-life — the Neve sound. Boosts sound big and beautiful, cuts sound natural. Choose over API EQs when you want warmth (API = punch, Neve = warmth). Choose over SSL EQ when you want color over precision. Best for: drums (legendary on kick and snare), vocals, bass, electric guitars — anything that benefits from that big, warm, musical Neve character.

name: Scheps Omni Channel 2
description: Comprehensive channel strip by mix engineer Andrew Scheps. Sections: Preamp (with saturation/drive), HPF/LPF, 4-band EQ, Compressor (VCA-style), De-Esser, Gate, Insert point (for other plugins). Each section can be reordered in the signal chain. Character: modern, flexible — designed as a complete channel solution. Choose when you want a fully-featured modern channel strip with maximum flexibility. Best for: complete channel processing on any source, modern mix workflows, any track needing EQ + compression + de-essing + gating in one plugin.

name: Scheps Parallel Particles
description: Parallel processing effect by Andrew Scheps. Adds four parallel processing layers: Sub (low-end), Air (high-end shimmer), Bite (mid-range presence), and Thick (density/fullness). Controls: per-layer Amount, global Mix. Character: additive enhancement — each layer adds a new dimension without changing the original. Choose when you want to enhance specific frequency/character ranges without EQ. Best for: drums (adding sub weight and air simultaneously), vocals (bite + air), mix bus (all four), guitars, any source needing enhancement without traditional EQ/compression.

name: Sibilance
description: Intelligent de-esser with organic, transparent sibilance control. Uses real-time sibilance detection (not simple threshold-based). Controls: Sensitivity (detection), Range (attenuation amount), Monitor. Character: the most natural-sounding de-esser — handles sibilance without the 'lisping' artifacts of traditional de-essers. Choose over DeEsser and RDeEsser when you want the most transparent results. Best for: vocals (the best de-esser for natural results), podcast de-essing, any vocal recording where sibilance control must be completely invisible.

name: Sibilance-Live
description: Low-latency version of Sibilance for live vocal processing. Same intelligent de-essing with minimal delay. Best for: live vocal de-essing, real-time vocal processing, live broadcast.

name: Silk Vocal
description: AI-powered vocal processor for smooth, polished vocal tone. Uses machine learning to automatically enhance vocal clarity, warmth, and presence. Controls: Intensity, Character mode. Character: smooth, polished, modern — intelligent vocal sweetening. Choose when you want AI-assisted vocal enhancement. Best for: quick vocal polish, modern pop vocal production, podcasts, voiceover, any vocal needing fast, intelligent enhancement.

name: Smack Attack
description: Transient designer for controlling attack (punch) and sustain (body/ring) independently. Controls: Attack (increase or decrease), Sustain (increase or decrease), Sensitivity, Duration. Character: changes the envelope shape without affecting EQ — boosts or reduces attack impact and sustain tail. Choose over compression when you want to change the 'shape' of a sound without compressing. Best for: drums (the #1 use — adding punch to kick/snare or reducing ring), percussion, acoustic guitar (reducing pick attack), bass (adding or reducing finger noise), any transient-rich source.

name: SoundShifter Pitch
description: Real-time pitch shifter with high-quality time-domain processing. Controls: Pitch shift (semitones + cents), Delay, Feedback, Mix. Maintains timing while shifting pitch. Character: clean pitch shifting. Best for: pitch correction, harmonizing (shift + mix with dry), creative pitch effects, octave doubling, sound design.

name: Space Rider
description: Automatic reverb level rider that dynamically adjusts wet/dry reverb mix based on input level. When input is loud, reverb decreases; when quiet, reverb increases — maintaining consistent perceived reverb regardless of dynamics. Controls: Target, Range, Speed. Character: intelligent reverb management. Choose when reverb is either too quiet during loud parts or too loud during quiet parts. Best for: vocals (essential for maintaining consistent reverb presence), dialogue, any dynamically varying source with reverb.

name: StudioVerse Audio Effects
description: Plugin platform for loading StudioVerse community-created effect chains. Access thousands of user-created signal processing chains and presets shared by the community. Choose when you want to explore community-created processing chains. Best for: discovering new processing approaches, quickly trying different effect combinations, learning from other engineers' signal chains.

name: Sub Align
description: Subwoofer alignment and phase correction tool for aligning subwoofer timing with main speakers. Controls: Delay, Phase, Polarity, HPF/LPF. Essential for live sound and studio monitoring. Character: transparent alignment — corrects timing without coloring sound. Best for: live sound (essential for sub alignment), studio sub alignment, ensuring proper sub-to-main speaker phase relationship.

name: Submarine
description: Sub-bass synthesizer generating deep sub-harmonics from existing audio content. Creates sub-bass frequencies BELOW the original fundamental using subharmonic synthesis. Controls: SubFreq (target frequency), Drive, Mix, Filter. Different from MaxxBass/RBass (which generate upper harmonics for perceived bass) — Submarine generates actual deep sub content. Choose when you need real sub-bass that doesn't exist in the recording. Best for: EDM (adding massive sub-bass to drops), hip-hop (808-style sub-bass enhancement), kick drums (adding sub weight), any source needing deep, physical sub-bass.

name: SuperTap 2-Taps
description: 2-tap delay with independent control per tap. Each tap: Delay time (free/sync), Feedback, Pan, Level, Filter, Modulation. Character: precise, flexible rhythmic delay. Choose over H-Delay when you need independent control over 2 delay taps with per-tap filtering and panning. Best for: stereo delay effects, ping-pong with filtering, creating specific rhythmic delay patterns with 2 taps.

name: SuperTap 6-Taps
description: 6-tap delay with independent control per tap — the most flexible delay for complex rhythmic patterns. Each tap: Delay time, Feedback, Pan, Level, Filter, Modulation, Rotation. Character: complex, rhythmic, evolving delay patterns. Choose when you need highly complex delay patterns with 6 independently controlled repeats. Best for: complex rhythmic delays, ambient guitar textures, creating polyrhythmic delay patterns, creative delay sound design, dub-style effects.

name: TRACT
description: System alignment and room correction EQ with real-time analysis. Measures room/system response and creates corrective EQ curves. Controls: measurement display, parametric EQ bands, target curve. Character: corrective — designed to fix system/room problems. Best for: PA system tuning, studio room correction, live sound system alignment, monitor optimization.

name: TRACT LinPhase
description: Linear-phase version of TRACT system alignment EQ. Same room/system correction with zero phase distortion. Choose over standard TRACT when phase accuracy matters. Best for: studio monitor correction (where phase matters), critical monitoring alignment, mastering room correction.

name: Torque
description: Drum tuning and tone-shaping plugin. Changes the apparent pitch of drums WITHOUT affecting timing or transients. Controls: Torque (pitch shift amount), Focus (frequency range of pitch change), Speed (how fast the tuning change happens), Mix. Character: natural-sounding pitch shifting designed specifically for drums. Choose when drums are tuned to the wrong key or need pitch adjustments. Best for: tuning kick and snare to song key, fixing drum tuning inconsistencies, creative drum tone reshaping, tuning toms, adjusting drum pitch without re-recording.

name: Torque-Live
description: Low-latency version of Torque for live drum processing. Same drum pitch-shifting with minimal delay. Best for: live drum tuning, real-time drum tone correction during live performance.

name: TransX Multi
description: Multi-band transient designer. Controls attack and sustain independently across multiple frequency bands. Each band: Attack, Sustain, Sensitivity. Character: frequency-selective transient shaping. Choose over TransX Wide when you need different transient settings for different frequency ranges (e.g., boost high-frequency attack while reducing low-frequency sustain). Best for: complex drum mixes (shape kick attack differently from cymbal attack), mastering transient control, any source needing frequency-dependent envelope shaping.

name: TransX Wide
description: Full-range transient designer. Controls: Attack (increase/decrease), Sustain (increase/decrease), Sensitivity, Range. Affects the entire frequency range equally. Character: simple, effective envelope shaping. Choose over Smack Attack for a slightly different algorithm, or TransX Multi when you don't need multiband. Best for: drums (adding/removing punch and ring), percussion, acoustic instruments, quick transient shaping on any percussive source.

name: TrueVerb
description: Room simulator reverb combining direct sound (early reflections) with reverb tail. Unique visual room display shows dimensions and source/listener positions. Controls: Room dimensions, Absorption, Distance, Decay, Damping, Pre-Delay, Mix, plus EQ. Character: natural, realistic room simulation — emphasis on realistic space rather than beautiful effect. Choose when you want to simulate a specific physical room rather than an idealized reverb effect. Best for: post-production (realistic room recreation), film/TV mixing, making tracks sound like they were recorded in a specific space, natural room ambience.

name: UltraPitch 3 Voices
description: 3-voice pitch shifter for harmonizing and thickening. Each voice: Pitch shift (semitones + cents), Delay, Pan, Level, Feedback, Formant correction. Creates 3 independent pitch-shifted copies. Character: clean pitch shifting with formant preservation. Best for: vocal harmonizing (3-part), thickening with micro-detuning, creative pitch effects, octave layering.

name: UltraPitch 6 Voices
description: 6-voice pitch shifter for rich harmonizing. Six independent pitch-shifted voices with full per-voice control. Character: lush, complex harmonizing and ensemble effects. Choose over 3-voice when you need richer harmonies or more voices. Best for: complex vocal harmonies (full chords), creating thick ensemble effects, choir simulation, dense pitch-shifted textures.

name: UltraPitch Shift
description: Single-voice pitch shifter for precise pitch adjustment. Controls: Pitch (semitones + cents), Delay, Feedback, Mix, Formant correction. Character: clean pitch shifting. Best for: basic pitch correction, single-voice harmony, octave doubling, sound design pitch effects.

name: VComp
description: Modeled vintage tube compressor based on classic tube compressor topology. Controls: Input, Attack (slow), Release (slow), Limit, Output, Character. Character: warm, smooth, slow — gentle tube compression with rich harmonics. Choose over modern compressors when you want slow, warm tube compression with vintage character. Best for: bus compression (gentle tube warmth), mastering (subtle tube limiting), vocals (warm compression), any source benefiting from slow, warm dynamics.

name: VEQ3
description: Modeled Neve 1073 3-band EQ — one of the most revered console EQs ever made. 3 bands: LF shelf (35/60/110/220Hz), MF peak (360Hz-7.2kHz), HF shelf (12kHz fixed). HPF (50/80/160/300Hz). Character: warm, big, musical — the classic Neve sound. Boosts add warmth and size, cuts sound natural. Choose over VEQ4 when 3 bands is sufficient (the 1073 is generally preferred for its simplicity). Best for: drums, bass, vocals, guitars — the most musical EQ for adding warmth and character.

name: VEQ4
description: Modeled Neve 1081 4-band EQ — extended version of the Neve console EQ with 4 bands. Bands: LF shelf, LMF parametric, HMF parametric, HF shelf. HPF/LPF. Character: same warm Neve character as VEQ3 but with extra mid band for more detailed control. Choose over VEQ3 when you need 4 bands of Neve EQ (more detailed mid sculpting). Best for: same as VEQ3 but when you need more midrange control — complex sources, detailed tonal work while maintaining Neve warmth.

name: VU Meter
description: Classic VU meter emulation with traditional needle-style display. VU ballistics (300ms integration time) show average level, not peaks. METERING TOOL ONLY — no audio processing. Best for: gain staging (VU meters show average loudness better than peak meters), vintage-style level monitoring, understanding dynamic range.

name: Vitamin
description: 5-band multiband harmonic enhancer. Each band (Low, Low-Mid, Mid, High-Mid, High) has independent Drive (harmonic generation) and Level controls plus Solo. Can generate harmonics in specific frequency ranges independently. Character: flexible enhancement — from subtle warmth in the lows to airy sparkle in the highs. Choose over broadband saturation when you want frequency-selective harmonic enhancement. Best for: adding sub weight + air simultaneously, enhancing specific bands without affecting others, mastering harmonic enhancement, mix bus sparkle, drums (sub weight + attack presence).

name: Vocal Bender
description: Real-time vocal pitch and formant manipulation. Shifts pitch and formant independently — pitch changes the note while formant changes the vocal character (gender, size). Controls: Pitch (semitones + cents), Formant (shift character), MIDI input for real-time control. Character: creative vocal transformation. Choose for creative vocal effects beyond standard pitch correction. Best for: gender transformation, character creation, vocal sound design, creating chipmunk/deep voice effects, EDM vocal manipulation.

name: Vocal Rider
description: Automatic vocal level rider that maintains consistent vocal volume using intelligent gain adjustment. Analyzes vocal dynamics and rides the fader in real-time to keep the vocal at a consistent level — like having an engineer ride the fader for you. Controls: Target range (min/max gain), Sensitivity, Rider speed, Music sidechain (ducks vocal less when music is quiet). Character: transparent — adjusts level without compression artifacts. Choose over compressor when you want level consistency without changing the vocal's dynamic character. Best for: lead vocals (essential — the #1 vocal tool for level consistency), dialogue, podcasts, voiceover, any vocal recording with inconsistent levels. Use BEFORE compression in the chain.

name: Voltage Amps Bass
description: Bass amplifier simulator with multiple amp models covering classic bass tones. Amp types: Clean, Warm, Driven, Modern. Controls: Gain, EQ, Volume, Cabinet select. Character: varies by model — from clean studio bass to driven rock bass. Best for: bass guitar DI recordings needing amp character, bass re-amping, synth bass needing amp warmth.

name: Voltage Amps Guitar
description: Guitar amplifier simulator with multiple amp models. Includes various amp voicings from clean to high-gain plus speaker cabinet modeling. Controls: Amp select, Gain, EQ, Volume, Cabinet. Best for: guitar DI recordings, re-amping, direct recording without real amps, quick guitar tone shaping.

name: W43
description: Modeled vintage noise reduction processor. Emulates the sound of the analog noise reduction circuitry with its characteristic frequency response coloration. Character: colored — adds the unique tonal imprint of vintage noise reduction systems. Best for: creative tonal coloring, vintage sound character, adding the 'encoded' sound of analog noise reduction.

name: WLM Meter
description: Loudness metering plugin compliant with ITU-R BS.1770, EBU R128, ATSC A/85, and other broadcast standards. Displays: Momentary loudness, Short-term loudness, Integrated loudness (LUFS), True Peak. METERING TOOL ONLY. Best for: broadcast compliance (essential), streaming platform loudness targeting, mastering to loudness standards, film/TV delivery compliance.

name: WLM Plus
description: Advanced loudness metering with extended features over WLM Meter. Adds: Loudness Range (LRA), True Peak measurement with inter-sample peak detection, multiple standard presets, logging. METERING TOOL ONLY. Best for: professional broadcast compliance, detailed loudness analysis, mastering to multiple delivery standards, archive loudness documentation.

name: WNS
description: Waves Noise Suppressor — multi-frequency noise gate. Instead of gating the entire signal, WNS uses multiple frequency-specific gates to suppress noise in specific bands while leaving clean frequencies untouched. Controls: per-band threshold, overall sensitivity. Character: more transparent than full-band gating. Choose over simple gate for complex noise situations where gating causes audible artifacts. Best for: dialogue with complex noise, live recordings with varying noise, situations where a simple gate chops the signal unnaturally.

name: Waves Gemstones
description: Creative multi-effects processor with multiple processing modules chained together. Various effect types available in a modular interface. Character: creative, experimental. Best for: creative processing, experimentation, discovering unusual effect combinations.

name: Waves Harmony
description: Real-time vocal harmony generator. Creates harmonies from a single vocal track based on MIDI or chord input. Multiple voices with independent level, pan, and formant control. Automatic voice-leading based on chord progressions. Character: realistic vocal harmonies in real-time. Choose when you need harmonies without recording additional vocal takes. Best for: creating background harmonies from a lead vocal, live performance harmonizing, quick harmony production, songwriter demos.

name: Waves Stream Receive
description: Audio streaming receiver for routing audio over local network. Receives audio from Waves Stream Send on another computer. Low-latency audio networking. UTILITY TOOL for audio routing. Best for: multi-computer setups, audio networking between machines.

name: Waves Stream Send
description: Audio streaming transmitter for sending audio over local network to Waves Stream Receive. Low-latency audio networking. UTILITY TOOL for audio routing. Best for: multi-computer setups, sending audio between machines.

name: Waves Tune
description: Full-featured pitch correction with graphical note editing. Displays detected notes on a piano-roll-style interface for manual editing. Controls: Speed (correction rate), Note transition, Tolerance, Vibrato control, Formant correction. Character: transparent to obvious depending on Speed setting — from invisible correction to the 'auto-tune effect'. Choose over Waves Tune Real-Time when you need visual editing and precision. Best for: studio vocal tuning (the standard workflow), detailed pitch correction with visual feedback, creating the auto-tune effect with Speed at fastest.

name: Waves Tune LT
description: Lightweight automatic pitch correction. Simplified real-time tuning with: Key/Scale select, Speed (correction rate), Note transition. Character: simple, effective — set key and speed, it tunes. Choose over full Waves Tune for quick, set-and-forget tuning. Best for: quick vocal tuning, live-ish recordings needing basic correction, songs where you just need to set key and let it work.

name: Waves Tune Real-Time
description: Zero-latency automatic pitch correction for live performance. Real-time tuning with no processing delay. Controls: Key/Scale, Speed, Tolerance, Vibrato. Character: from transparent to heavy auto-tune effect depending on speed. Choose over studio Waves Tune for live performance (zero latency). Best for: live vocal tuning, real-time pitch correction during recording, live performance, monitoring with pitch correction.

name: X-Click
description: Click and pop remover for vinyl transfers and damaged audio. Detects and removes impulsive noise artifacts (clicks, pops, crackle) using intelligent detection. Controls: Threshold, Sensitivity, Click type. Character: transparent — removes only clicks without affecting program material. Best for: vinyl record transfers, restoring click-damaged recordings, cleaning up old tape recordings with splicing clicks, audio restoration.

name: X-Crackle
description: Crackle and surface noise remover for vinyl transfers. Targets continuous low-level surface noise and crackle that X-Click doesn't address. Controls: Threshold, Sensitivity, Reduction amount. Character: transparent noise reduction for continuous surface noise. Best for: vinyl record restoration (use after X-Click), removing surface noise from old recordings, cleaning up archival audio.

name: X-FDBK
description: Real-time feedback elimination for live sound. Detects feedback frequencies as they develop and places precise notch filters to prevent feedback before it becomes audible. Automatic and manual modes. Controls: sensitivity, number of available filters, detection speed. Character: transparent — notch filters are surgical. Best for: live sound (essential feedback control), stage monitor systems, any amplified sound system prone to feedback.

name: X-Hum
description: Hum remover targeting 50/60Hz electrical hum and its harmonics. Identifies fundamental hum frequency and places notch filters at the fundamental plus harmonics. Controls: Fundamental frequency (50/60Hz), Number of harmonics, Filter Q, Learn mode. Character: surgical — removes only hum frequencies. Best for: recordings with ground loop hum, electrical hum from guitar amps, AC hum in vintage recordings, any recording contaminated with 50 or 60Hz hum.

name: X-Noise
description: Broadband noise reduction using noise profiling. Learns the noise characteristics of a recording, then subtracts it from the signal. Controls: Threshold, Reduction, Attack, Release, Learn mode (capture noise profile). Character: effective but can introduce artifacts at extreme settings — 'musical noise' or watery artifacts. Choose over Z-Noise for simpler workflow. Choose NS1 for fastest one-knob approach. Best for: reducing steady-state noise (hiss, room tone, HVAC), studio recordings with background noise, audio restoration, any recording with consistent background noise.

name: Z-Noise
description: Advanced noise reduction with real-time adaptive noise profiling. Unlike X-Noise (which uses a static noise profile), Z-Noise continuously adapts to changing noise floors. Controls: Threshold, Reduction, Attack, Release, Sensitivity, Adaptive profiling controls. Character: more transparent than X-Noise for changing noise environments — adapts in real-time. Choose over X-Noise when noise level fluctuates. Choose over Clarity Vx for non-vocal sources. Best for: live recordings with varying noise, field recordings, dialogue with changing background noise, any source where the noise floor is not constant.

name: dbx-160
description: Modeled dbx 160 VCA compressor — the most aggressive, punchy compressor in the collection. Hard-knee VCA compression with that distinctive dbx 'snap'. Controls: Threshold, Ratio (1:1-inf:1, all hard-knee), Output Gain. Character: aggressive, tight, snappy, punchy — very fast VCA response with hard knee creates a distinctive 'slap' on transients. Choose over CLA-76 when you want even more aggressive, harder-hitting compression. Choose for that specific 'dbx' snappy character. Best for: drums (the classic 80s drum sound — Phil Collins, etc.), snare (extreme snap), bass (tight control), synths (aggressive pumping), parallel compression (crush with dbx, blend with dry). NOT for gentle or transparent compression.
